locations.name: Bergisel Ski Jump
locations.setting: Zaha Hadid's 2002 ski jump tower on Innsbruck's Bergisel hill, combining a competition in-run and judging tower with a public viewing platform and cafe over the city.

locations.name: Bregenz Festival House
locations.setting: A lakeside festival hall on Lake Constance, home of the Bregenz Festival's floating stage and indoor auditorium, backed by mountain views.

locations.name: Burgtheater
locations.setting: Austria's national theatre on the Ringstrasse, a grand 19th-century building with ceremonial staircases, foyers and a horseshoe-shaped auditorium.

locations.name: Erzberg
locations.setting: Open-pit iron ore mine near Eisenerz with terraced orange slopes over 700 metres high, a tourist park offering truck and cable tours through the workings, and host to the annual Erzbergrodeo enduro race.
locations.facilities: The Bohrerschmiede event space accommodates up to 100 people (own site).

locations.name: Flughafen Wien Aspern (Seestadt)
locations.setting: The site of Vienna's historic Aspern airfield, now redeveloped as the Seestadt district, retaining some early aviation-era structures amid new urban blocks.

locations.name: Gasometer Vienna
locations.setting: Four former 19th-century gasholders in Vienna's Simmering district, rebuilt with glass domes into apartments, offices, a shopping mall, cinema and event hall around their original brick shells.
locations.facilities: Tower A commercial space available from 30 sqm, from EUR 16 per sqm net; concert hall capacity up to 4,200 visitors with more than 100 events a year; over 22,000 sqm of shopping area on site (own site).
locations.logistics: U3 subway station Gasometer on site; on-site parking garage with 1,100 spaces, first 1.5 hours free (own site).

locations.name: Hallstatt
locations.setting: Lakeside Alpine village of stacked wooden and stucco houses between the Hallstatter See and a steep mountainside, reachable by funicular to the salt mine above.

locations.name: Hangar-7
locations.setting: Curved glass and steel aviation hangar at Salzburg Airport housing the Flying Bulls historic aircraft collection, a restaurant and event spaces beneath its open-span dome roof.

locations.name: Hotel Sacher Vienna
locations.setting: Grand 1876 hotel opposite the State Opera, with red-panelled parlours, a chandeliered dining room and the original Sachertorte kitchen.

locations.name: Justizpalast Wien
locations.setting: Vienna's historicist Palace of Justice, seat of the supreme and administrative courts, with a monumental stone facade and galleried central hall.

locations.name: Karl-Marx-Hof
locations.setting: A monumental 1920s municipal housing block from Vienna's Red Vienna period, stretching over a kilometre with arched gateways, courtyards and a reddish facade.

locations.name: Kirche am Steinhof (Klinik Penzing)
locations.setting: Otto Wagner's Art Nouveau hospital church of 1907 crowning a hillside campus of pavilion wards built for the former Lower Austrian asylum, now Vienna's Klinik Penzing.

locations.name: Kitzbühel
locations.setting: Alpine market town below the Hahnenkamm and Kitzbueheler Horn, with a pastel-fronted medieval centre and ski infrastructure running from the streets onto the pistes.

locations.name: Kunsthaus Graz
locations.setting: Biomorphic blue-panelled contemporary art museum of 2003 on the Mur riverbank, its bulging acrylic shell fitted with roof-top nozzle skylights beside Graz's baroque old town.
locations.facilities: Rentable spaces named on site are Space04 (meeting/presentation room) and Needle (elevated glass observation platform) (own site).

locations.name: Museum Arbeitswelt Steyr
locations.setting: Museum of industrial and labour history housed in a former weapons and bicycle factory hall in Steyr's Wehrgraben quarter, with original machine-hall interiors.
locations.price_note: Venue hire from EUR 190 for a half day (up to 6 hours, Seminar Room 2) up to EUR 1,460 for a full day (Large Hall), prices exclude 20% VAT, valid through 31 December 2026 (own site).
locations.facilities: Rooms: Large Hall 380 sqm, Small Hall 140 sqm, Seminar Room 1 80 sqm, Seminar Room 2 60 sqm, Gallery 270 sqm; evening surcharge after 20:00 of EUR 65 per hour; setup on the day before costs 30% of the room rate (own site).

locations.name: Naschmarkt
locations.setting: A 1.5-kilometre open-air market along the Wienzeile with produce stalls, delicatessens and restaurants, and a Saturday flea market at its western end.

locations.name: Salzburg Old Town
locations.setting: Baroque old town of church domes, squares and narrow lanes beneath the Hohensalzburg fortress on the Salzach river.

locations.name: Sanatorium Purkersdorf
locations.setting: An early modernist sanatorium building from 1905 on the edge of the Vienna Woods, with a clean white geometric facade, now used for events.

photo.author: derivative work: Alberto Fernandez Fernandez (talk) Sanatoriumpurkersdorf1.JPG: Roman Klementschitz, Wien

locations.name: Schönbrunn Palace
locations.setting: Baroque imperial summer palace with more than 1,400 rooms, formal gardens, the Gloriette hilltop folly and a historic zoo.
locations.price_note: Outdoor motion pictures or commercial projects from EUR 6,600 per day (incl. 20% VAT), minimum fee. Smaller outdoor documentaries and travel reports: EUR 333 per hour (incl. 13% VAT). Indoor filming beyond private use: EUR 333 per hour for smaller productions; large-scale indoor productions on request. Prices valid from 27 March 2026 (own site).
locations.suitability: Filming beyond private use requires prior written approval from the Schonbrunn Group, requested at least 3 weeks ahead. Indoor filming beyond private use is only allowed outside regular opening hours: battery-powered lighting only (max 12V per head, 100V total), flash photography is prohibited, and furniture may not be moved. Outdoor filming for private purposes needs no approval, but drones, barriers and climbing on structures are not allowed in the park (own site).

locations.name: Semmering Railway
locations.setting: The world's first standard-gauge mountain railway, opened in 1854, still an operating OBB main line with sixteen tunnels and stone viaducts climbing the Semmering pass.

locations.name: Sölden
locations.setting: High Alpine ski resort village in the Ötztal valley with glacier roads climbing to 2,800 metres and a summit restaurant at 3,048 metres.

locations.name: Tabakfabrik Linz
locations.setting: A converted 1935 Bauhaus-style tobacco factory in Linz, now a creative and start-up quarter with exhibition halls, event spaces and a rooftop terrace across the Danube from the old town.

locations.name: University of Vienna Main Building
locations.setting: Historicist university building of 1884 on the Ringstrasse, with an arcaded courtyard of scholars' monuments, a grand ceremonial hall and lecture theatres.

locations.name: Vienna City Hall (Rathaus)
locations.setting: Neo-Gothic seat of Vienna's city government from 1883, with a vaulted arcaded courtyard, ceremonial halls and a square in front used for open-air events and markets.

locations.name: Vienna State Opera
locations.setting: An 1869 opera house on the Ringstrasse with a gilded auditorium, grand staircase and backstage areas that host around 350 performances a season.

locations.name: Volksoper Wien
locations.setting: Vienna's second opera house, a late-19th-century theatre staging opera, operetta and musicals, with a traditional gilded auditorium and backstage areas.

locations.name: Wiener Riesenrad (Prater)
locations.setting: A 1897 giant Ferris wheel and adjoining amusement park on the edge of the Prater, with vintage gondola cabins and a fairground of rides, food stalls and an events hall.

locations.name: Wiener Stadthalle
locations.setting: Vienna's largest multi-purpose arena, opened in 1958, with several halls used for concerts, sport and exhibitions under a distinctive folded roof.

photo.author: No machine-readable author provided. Extrawurst assumed (based on copyright claims).

locations.name: Wörthersee
locations.setting: A 19-kilometre subalpine lake ringed by resort towns, promenades, lidos and wooded hills between Klagenfurt and Velden.

locations.name: WU Vienna Library and Learning Center
locations.setting: The library building of Vienna's business university campus, a deconstructivist design by Zaha Hadid with sweeping concrete forms and glass atria.

locations.name: Abattoir, Anderlecht
locations.setting: Historic livestock market and food-hall complex in Anderlecht, Brussels, with weekend markets, the FOODMET food hall and renovated buildings used for events.

locations.name: Abdij van Herkenrode
locations.setting: A former Cistercian abbey site on the edge of Hasselt with a walled herb garden, monastic outbuildings and a restored gatehouse.

locations.name: Alden Biesen Castle
locations.setting: Moated former headquarters of the Teutonic Order in Bilzen with formal gardens and a museum, now a conference and cultural centre that lists availability for film shoots.
locations.suitability: Website lists availability for film shooting alongside conferences and events.

locations.name: Ancienne Belgique (AB)
locations.setting: Concert hall on Boulevard Anspach in central Brussels with two stages, offering the venue for private hire and running its own in-house production and photography team.
locations.facilities: Six rentable spaces: AB Connect 126 sqm (20-60 guests), AB Salon 63 sqm (54-110 guests), AB Antenna 145 sqm (50-120 guests), AB Rooftop 84 sqm (50-80 guests), AB Club 170 sqm (100-280 guests), AB Main Hall 442 sqm (500-2000 guests standing). Basic furniture (tables, chairs, reception tables) is included; technical support available for lighting, sound, projection and stage setup; wheelchair accessible.
locations.suitability: Recording and livestreaming is possible in the Main Hall, AB Club and AB Salon using a fixed camera setup (separate technical specifications document available on request).
locations.logistics: About 10 minutes' walk from Brussels Central Station; accessible by public transport or car.

locations.name: Aquatopia
locations.setting: A municipal indoor swimming pool complex in Aalst with a sports basin, recreational pools and slides used by local clubs and schools.

locations.name: Autoworld
locations.setting: Vintage and classic car museum in the Cinquantenaire park's Belvedere hall in Brussels, hired out as an event space for more than a thousand guests.
locations.facilities: Event space for over 1,000 guests among the car collection, with escape-game and audio-guide experiences.

locations.name: Bois du Cazier
locations.setting: Former coal mine at Marcinelle near Charleroi with preserved headframes and pithead buildings, site of the 1956 mining disaster, now housing industry and glass museums.

locations.name: Bozar
locations.setting: Centre for Fine Arts in central Brussels hosting concerts, exhibitions and film screenings across several halls, with a dedicated team for private and corporate venue hire.

locations.name: Bruges Historic Centre
locations.setting: Intact medieval city centre of canals, cobbled streets, stepped-gable brick houses and the towering thirteenth-century Belfry.

locations.name: C-mine
locations.setting: Former Winterslag coalmine in Genk with preserved headframes and a compressor hall, now a creative cluster of more than 30 spaces that are rented out for events.

locations.name: Château de Freÿr
locations.setting: Renaissance chateau on a bend of the Meuse near Hastière with terraced 18th-century gardens, whose barn and orangeries can be booked for events.

locations.name: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
locations.setting: Seven-kilometre motor racing circuit through the Ardennes hills near Francorchamps, host of the Formula 1 Belgian Grand Prix, with the track and facilities available to hire for private and business events.

locations.name: Citadel of Namur
locations.setting: Hilltop fortress complex above Namur spanning two thousand years of military building, with underground passages, a park and rooms offered for professional and private hire.
locations.facilities: Four rentable spaces in the former Terra Nova barracks (Salle Blanche, Salle Don Juan, Salle Vauban, and a bar), each accommodating up to 120 people, plus a professional kitchen with cold rooms, freezer, hood, gas hobs, fryers, ovens, dishwasher and sinks. Furniture, screen, WiFi, cleaning (except kitchen and bar) and electricity/water/heating are included. Equipment rental: standing tables EUR 15 each, flipchart with paper EUR 30, sound equipment EUR 60, video projector EUR 75.
locations.logistics: EUR 200 deposit required per room; site visits by appointment Monday-Thursday, 9am-5pm.

locations.name: De Grote Post
locations.setting: A former central post office in Oostende converted into a cultural centre with a concert hall, library and cafe behind its restored mid-century facade.

locations.name: Doel
locations.setting: Polder village on the Scheldt earmarked for demolition since the 1990s to expand the port of Antwerp, now with around 200 empty houses, street art and a small remaining community.

locations.name: Flagey
locations.setting: 1938 Art Deco former national radio building on Place Sainte-Croix in Brussels, now a music and cinema centre with studios and halls available for venue hire.

locations.name: Grand Hospice
locations.setting: A large nineteenth-century former almshouse in central Brussels with a neoclassical facade, an arcaded courtyard and long institutional corridors, now partly used for housing.
locations.facilities: Entrance hall, corridors, interior courtyard, garden, carriage entrance

locations.name: Grand-Hornu
locations.setting: Neoclassical former colliery and workers' town near Mons, built 1810 to 1830 around an oval courtyard, now a design and contemporary art centre with rooms available for hire.

locations.name: Gravensteen
locations.setting: Moated twelfth-century stone castle with towers, battlements and a gatehouse standing in the middle of Ghent.
locations.facilities: Knights' Hall (Ridderzaal) seats up to 99 people; the Suikerlade room is also bookable. Used for meetings, performances, lectures, presentations and receptions.
locations.suitability: Available for hire outside the castle's normal opening hours.

locations.name: Halles de Schaerbeek
locations.setting: Former covered market hall in Schaerbeek, Brussels, converted into a performing arts venue for dance and theatre, with its hall offered for hire.
locations.price_note: Great Hall EUR 10,000/day (EUR 5,000/day for community organisations); Small Hall EUR 2,000/day (EUR 1,000/day community); Cellar/former swimming pool EUR 1,000/day (EUR 500/day community) (own site).
locations.facilities: Three rentable spaces: Great Hall 1200 sqm (up to 2000 people standing, sit-down or buffet dining possible); Small Hall 215 sqm (400 standing / 120 seated, includes stage and bar); Cellar/former swimming pool 400 sqm including a 100 sqm room 6m deep (up to 300 people, foyer with bar).
locations.suitability: Venue hosts concerts, markets and conferences; explicitly does not accommodate private parties such as birthdays or weddings.

locations.name: Handelsbeurs Concert Hall
locations.setting: 19th-century former merchants' exchange on the Kouter in Ghent, now a concert hall with a brasserie, offering its hall for private hire.

locations.name: Hof van Liere (University of Antwerp city campus)
locations.setting: A restored Renaissance courtyard building on the University of Antwerp's city campus, with arcaded galleries and a walled garden used for lectures and events.

locations.name: Janseniustoren
locations.setting: A squat medieval defence tower on the banks of the Dijle in central Leuven, standing among old mill buildings and narrow riverside streets.

locations.name: K-Tower
locations.setting: A slender, diagonally tilted residential and office tower beside the Leie river in Kortrijk, built in the early 2010s as a landmark of the city's redevelopment.

locations.name: Kortrijk Xpo
locations.setting: 40,000 square metre exhibition and conference campus in Kortrijk with six halls and a covered boulevard connecting them, rented out for trade shows, conferences and public events.
locations.facilities: Six halls, a Meeting Center with five rooms, catering, ticketing, parking and technical support.

locations.name: Kursaal Oostende
locations.setting: Seafront concert and congress hall in Ostend with a large auditorium and casino, offering dedicated business and corporate event spaces.

locations.name: La Monnaie / De Munt
locations.setting: Belgium's national opera house in central Brussels, offering venue hire and audiovisual exploitation services alongside its main stage and the smaller Malibran room.

locations.name: Lites Studios
locations.setting: Modern studio complex near Brussels with five stages, including Europe's largest heated indoor water tank for underwater filming.
locations.facilities: Five sound stages from 170 to 1,700 m2 (Stage 1: 1,250 m2, Stage 2: 1,700 m2) and a 1,450 m2 water stage with a 24 x 21 m deep section, up to 10.8 m depth with the floor flooded, 7 million litres kept at 30 to 32 C, a moveable pool floor rated for 20 tonnes of set and a 14.3 m grid height. Dressing rooms and an in-house camera rental department.
locations.suitability: Sound stages with high acoustic performance; the water stage is used for underwater and surface filming with a tilting, submersible platform and dual gantry cranes. The studio points to Belgium's 45 percent tax incentive.
locations.logistics: Fabrieksstraat 81, 1800 Vilvoorde (Brussels)

locations.name: Loppem Castle
locations.setting: Neo-Gothic castle built in the 1850s and 1860s near Bruges with original interiors and art collections, whose former stables now form a hall for hire.
locations.facilities: Former stables converted into an event hall for 250 to 300 seated guests or 450 standing, plus vaulted cellars for smaller groups.

locations.name: Lycee Emile Max
locations.setting: An Art Nouveau public secondary school in Schaerbeek with an ornate wrought-iron staircase and entrance hall behind an understated brick facade.
locations.facilities: Wrought-iron staircase, exterior facade

locations.name: Paleis op de Meir
locations.setting: 1745 rococo mansion on Antwerp's main shopping street, once refurbished for Napoleon Bonaparte, now a heritage house offering rooms for dinners, receptions and meetings.

locations.name: Saint Peter's Abbey, Ghent
locations.setting: Former Benedictine abbey by Sint-Pietersplein in Ghent with a baroque church, historic cellars and a south-facing vineyard garden, whose rooms are hired for receptions and conferences.
locations.facilities: Historic cellar and loft rooms, courtyard and south-facing garden with vineyard, underground parking nearby.

locations.name: Sport Vlaanderen Gent (Wielercentrum)
locations.setting: An outdoor cycling centre in Ghent's Blaarmeersen sports park with a velodrome track, clubhouse and surrounding playing fields.

locations.name: Sport Vlaanderen Heusden-Zolder
locations.setting: A regional sports centre in Heusden-Zolder next to the Circuit Zolder racetrack, with an athletics track and multi-purpose sports halls.

locations.name: Sport Vlaanderen Hofstade
locations.setting: A public sports and recreation domain in Zemst with a swimming lake, athletics track and sports halls set among woodland.

locations.name: Sport Vlaanderen Waregem
locations.setting: A regional sports centre in Waregem with an athletics track, sports halls and outdoor pitches used for training and competitions.

locations.name: Sport Vlaanderen Willebroek
locations.setting: A national watersports centre on a canal in Willebroek with a straight regatta course, grandstands and boathouses used for rowing and canoe racing.

locations.name: Station Mechelen
locations.setting: A working railway station in central Mechelen with platforms, an overhead concourse and surrounding public squares, listed by Screen Flanders with filming requests handled by national rail operator NMBS.
locations.logistics: Filming requests are arranged directly with NMBS (national rail operator), not the station itself.

locations.name: Stoomcentrum Maldegem
locations.setting: Volunteer-run heritage railway based at Maldegem station, running historic steam and diesel trains through the Meetjesland countryside.
locations.suitability: Website explicitly offers photo and film location bookings alongside private charters and group visits.

locations.name: STUK, Leuven
locations.setting: Multidisciplinary arts centre on Naamsestraat in Leuven with theatre spaces, a cinema and studios, offering rooms and rehearsal spaces for rent.

locations.name: Tour & Taxis
locations.setting: Former customs and rail freight depot on the Brussels canal, with 19th-century brick, glass and iron warehouse halls now used as a large indoor event and exhibition venue.

locations.name: Tour a Plomb
locations.setting: A former lead-shot factory tower near Brussels' old abattoir district, now a community and sports centre that keeps its raw industrial brickwork and stairwells.
locations.facilities: Stairwells, exposed industrial interior

locations.name: Villa Empain
locations.setting: 1930s Art Deco mansion on Avenue Franklin Roosevelt in Brussels, home to the Boghossian Foundation, with salons, gardens and a bar that can be privatised for events.
locations.price_note: Filming from EUR 7,500; commercial shoots from EUR 5,000; wedding photography from EUR 1,500 (own site).
locations.suitability: Villa is offered for film shoots, promotional or commercial clips, and wedding photo shoots; filming is restricted to outside the venue's normal operating hours.

locations.name: Villers Abbey ruins
locations.setting: The roofless ruins of a Cistercian abbey near Villers-la-Ville, with vaulted cellars, a ruined church nave and monastic gardens open for shoots by arrangement.

locations.name: Brijuni National Park
locations.setting: An archipelago of fourteen islands off Fažana, the former summer residence of Josip Broz Tito, with parkland, a safari zone, Roman and Byzantine ruins and a residence complex.

locations.name: Church of St. Donatus
locations.setting: Circular ninth-century pre-Romanesque church built partly from recycled Roman stone on Zadar's ancient forum, now used as a concert venue for its acoustics.
locations.known_for: Through the Centuries (per Zadar Film Commission)

locations.name: Croatian National Theatre in Split
locations.setting: A neo-Renaissance national theatre building from 1893 in central Split, with a main stage, tiered auditorium and rehearsal rooms used for opera, drama and ballet.

locations.name: Croatian National Theatre Ivan pl. Zajc
locations.setting: Opera house opened in 1885 in central Rijeka with a gilded horseshoe auditorium, main stage and rehearsal rooms, still in daily use for opera, ballet and drama.

locations.name: Diocletian's Palace
locations.setting: Fourth-century Roman imperial palace whose walls, basement halls and peristyle form the living core of Split's old town, mixing ancient masonry with shops and homes.

locations.name: Dolac Market
locations.setting: Zagreb's main open-air produce market on a raised square above the central square, with rows of red umbrellas, fruit and vegetable stalls and an indoor hall, run by the city market company.

locations.name: Dražen Petrović Basketball Hall
locations.setting: Indoor arena at Zagreb's Cibona sports complex with seating for around 5,400, home court of KK Cibona and a regular venue for concerts and other events.

photo.author: Andrea Cislaghi from Robbio Lomellina, Italia

locations.name: Dubrovnik Old Town
locations.setting: Walled seaside old town with intact medieval ramparts, baroque stone streets and fortresses rising straight from the Adriatic.
locations.known_for: Game of Thrones (King's Landing, from season 2), Star Wars: The Last Jedi (2017), Robin Hood (2018)

locations.name: Esplanade Zagreb Hotel
locations.setting: Art Deco hotel opened in 1925 next to Zagreb's main station to serve Orient Express passengers, with a marble lobby, period ballroom and historic guest rooms.

locations.name: Franjo Tuđman Airport
locations.setting: Croatia's main international airport south of Zagreb, with a passenger terminal built in 2017, an aircraft apron, control tower and cargo facilities.

locations.name: Governor's Palace, Rijeka
locations.setting: A late 19th-century palace on Rijeka's waterfront built for the Hungarian-appointed governor, now housing the Maritime and History Museum of the Croatian Littoral.

locations.name: Hotel Kvarner (Grand Hotel Kvarner)
locations.setting: The first purpose-built hotel on the eastern Adriatic coast, opened in 1884 on Opatija's seafront, with a Belle Epoque facade, period function rooms and a sea-facing terrace.

locations.name: Jadran Film
locations.setting: Film studio founded in 1946 with stages and backlot grounds in Zagreb's Dubrava district, host to well over a hundred international co-productions.
locations.known_for: Winnetou series (1962-1968), The Tin Drum (1979), Sophie's Choice (1982)
locations.facilities: Nine stages totalling 8,000 m2; the largest are Studio 2 (1,200 m2, 47 x 23 m, over 10 m high) and Studio 4 (1,200 m2, 60 x 20 m, 8 m working height), with Studio 6-7 a divisible 950 m2 complex and Studio 9 a 440 m2 TV studio. A 1,000 m2 production hub with offices and its own transformer station, plus carpentry, paint, plaster and model workshops.
locations.suitability: Presented as a full-service production base with base camp infrastructure and dressing, makeup and wardrobe rooms around each stage; Studios 4 and 9 are on long-term lease to a television company and a 2,500 to 3,200 m2 Studio 10 is planned. Stage pages are marked under construction pending a summer 2026 relaunch.
locations.logistics: Ulica Rudolfa Kolaka 12, Zagreb; parking for production vehicles at Studio 2 and gated access with RF cards at the production hub.

locations.name: Kazalište Komedija
locations.setting: A musical theatre on Kaptol in Zagreb's old town, staging operettas, musicals and cabaret in a roughly 500-seat auditorium, operating since 1950.

locations.name: Kopački Rit Nature Park
locations.setting: A wetland nature park at the confluence of the Drava and Danube rivers, with flooded forest, reed beds, an observation tower and boat routes through the marshland.

locations.name: Krka National Park
locations.setting: Karst river canyon with a chain of travertine waterfalls, lakes and old watermills, plus the island monastery of Visovac reached only by boat.

locations.name: Lauba
locations.setting: Former Zagreb textile and later arms factory converted into an open art house, with a large column-free exhibition hall, glass additions and a sculpture garden.
locations.facilities: 1,350 sq m of exhibition space; the venue states it can host groups of 20 to 2,000 guests, for dinners, concerts, conferences, weddings, workshops, film screenings and theatre performances.

locations.name: Medvednica Nature Park
locations.setting: The forested mountain range above Zagreb, with the ruined medieval Medvedgrad fortress, a former ore mine open to visitors, hiking trails and the Sljeme peak and ski area.

locations.name: National and University Library in Zagreb
locations.setting: Croatia's national library, a large modernist building from 1995 with reading rooms, book stacks and a central atrium, serving as the country's main research library.

locations.name: Opatija
locations.setting: Belle-epoque resort town on the Kvarner riviera with a twelve-kilometre coastal promenade, villa gardens and grand hotels dating from the Austro-Hungarian era.

locations.name: Pag Salt Pans
locations.setting: Working saltworks on Pag island with roots in Roman times, laid out as shallow evaporation basins and canals, with a visitor centre run by the salt company Solana Pag.
locations.known_for: Following the Salt (documentary, per Zadar Film Commission)

locations.name: Plitvice Lakes National Park
locations.setting: Chain of sixteen terraced turquoise lakes linked by waterfalls in a forested karst canyon.
locations.known_for: Treasure of the Silver Lake (1962), Karl May Winnetou westerns (1962-1968)

locations.name: Port of Rijeka
locations.setting: Working deep-sea cargo port on the Kvarner Gulf with container terminals, cranes, warehouses and the older Delta basin quaysides close to the city centre.

locations.name: Pula Arena
locations.setting: Roman stone amphitheatre in central Pula whose surviving outer wall and tiered seating host summer concerts, the Pula Film Festival and other large outdoor events.
locations.price_note: Filming or event use for up to 30 minutes while the site stays open to the public: EUR 5,000 plus VAT; longer use that closes the amphitheatre to visitors is priced separately, per a document not published on the page (own site).
locations.suitability: Site states that using the amphitheatre for filming or events requires consent from the City of Pula, in addition to approval from the Conservation Department in Pula and the Archaeological Museum of Istria, which manages the venue.
locations.logistics: Requests for use up to 30 minutes must be submitted at least 15 days in advance to the Archaeological Museum of Istria (uprava.ami@gmail.com); use of over 30 minutes that closes the site to the public depends on the city's official annual event calendar, so approval cannot be guaranteed until that programme is announced.

locations.name: Rikard Benčić Complex
locations.setting: Former sugar refinery and later Rikard Benčić machine factory in central Rijeka, restored as an industrial heritage complex now housing the Rijeka City Museum.

locations.name: St. Nicholas Fortress
locations.setting: Triangular sixteenth-century sea fortress guarding the entrance to Šibenik's channel, a UNESCO World Heritage site reachable only by boat.

locations.name: Stadion Maksimir
locations.setting: Zagreb's largest football ground, home of GNK Dinamo Zagreb and the national team, with open bowl seating for more than 35,000 next to Maksimir Park.

locations.name: Veli Rat Lighthouse
locations.setting: Working stone lighthouse of 1849 at the northern tip of Dugi Otok, one of the tallest on the Adriatic, reached by a track through pine forest above a rocky cove.

locations.name: Zagreb Fair
locations.setting: Mid-twentieth-century trade fair ground south of the Sava with modernist exhibition pavilions, large halls and an open showground used for trade events year round.
locations.facilities: 132,000 sq m of pavilion space and 6,000 sq m of open-air space; the Technology Park occupies pavilion 12, at 5,000 sq m.

locations.name: Zagreb Main Railway Station
locations.setting: Zagreb's principal railway station, an 1892 Austro-Hungarian building on Tomislav Square with a domed main hall and platforms facing the city's museum quarter.

locations.name: Archbishop's Palace, Kroměříž
locations.setting: UNESCO-listed baroque archbishop's palace with opulent state rooms and formal gardens that have stood in for imperial Vienna.
locations.facilities: Sala terrena (full hall): up to 150 people (100 seated). Single hall of the Sala terrena: 70. Stucco Hall and Tiled Stove Hall: 50 (with chairs and tables). Cold-kitchen catering available. Adjacent to the Palace Garden (own site).
locations.suitability: The palace's own site notes that films have been shot there ('Filmovalo se u nas') (own site).

locations.name: Aviation Museum Kunovice
locations.setting: Aircraft collection and hangars at Kunovice airfield near Uherské Hradiště, on the site of the former Let Kunovice aircraft works, with propeller planes and gliders on display.

locations.name: Barrandov Studios
locations.setting: Prague studio complex dating from the early 1930s with large sound stages, extensive costume and prop stocks and backlot space.
locations.facilities: 14 soundproof stages totalling 10,900 m2 at Barrandov plus four at the Hostivar site, most with rigging pulley systems; permanent exterior sets include a 15,000 m2 medieval town with buildings up to 10 m and a 39 x 60 m Paris street with twenty facades and ten interiors. Production rooms, makeup and dressing rooms, wardrobe, camera and prop storage, catering spaces and a large costume and prop stock.
locations.suitability: Offers stage rental, set construction, costume and prop rental, dubbing and production support, with on-site firefighting services for pyrotechnics and high-risk scenes; the studio cites the Czech cash rebate of up to 35 percent.
locations.logistics: Barrandov site 10 minutes from Prague city centre and 15 minutes from Vaclav Havel Airport, Hostivar site 18 minutes from both; parking for cars and trucks on site. Website in Czech only.

locations.name: Bohnice Psychiatric Hospital
locations.setting: Pavilion-style psychiatric hospital campus opened in 1909 on a wooded hillside in north Prague, dozens of period brick buildings connected by paths and gardens, still in clinical use.
locations.price_note: Filming from CZK 5,000 per hour for interior, CZK 4,500 per hour for exterior, plus CZK 2,000 per hour for professional supervision (own site).
locations.facilities: Interior and exterior filming spaces are available within the hospital grounds (own site).
locations.suitability: Interior and exterior filming are permitted (own site).

locations.name: Brněnec Textile Factory
locations.setting: 19th century textile mill complex on the Svitava river in the village of Brněnec, with brick production halls, a chimney and former worker housing.

locations.name: Brno Exhibition Centre
locations.setting: Large trade fair and exhibition ground south-west of Brno's centre, with functionalist 1920s pavilions and modern halls used for conventions, concerts and filming.
locations.facilities: 14 exhibition halls (19 conference halls). Conference hall E1abc: theatre capacity 1,008, congress capacity 936. Conference hall Rotunda: theatre capacity 450. Smaller halls from 30 (theatre). Open-air areas from 1,797 to 12,809 sqm (paved, gravel or bituminous surface). Hall heights from 2.9 to 26.7 m (own site).
locations.logistics: On-site Expoparking service (own site).

locations.name: Budweiser Budvar Brewery
locations.setting: Working state brewery on the northern edge of Ceske Budejovice, with early 20th century brick brewhouses, cellars, bottling lines and a visitor centre offering plant tours.

locations.name: Café Louvre
locations.setting: Grand 1902 Art Nouveau café on Národní street in Prague, with a billiard room and tall windows over the street, run continuously except for a closure during the communist period.

locations.name: Český Krumlov
locations.setting: Renaissance and baroque town wrapped in a tight bend of the Vltava river beneath a painted castle tower.
locations.known_for: The Adventures of Pinocchio (1996), Hostel (2005), The Illusionist (2006)

locations.name: Cheb Railway Station
locations.setting: Historic railway station in the west Bohemian border town of Cheb, with period platforms and a station building listed by the national film commission as a filming location.

locations.name: Coal and Water Storage Tower Vratislavice
locations.setting: Early 20th century coaling station and water tower on the edge of Liberec, with a 75 metre boiler chimney and a steam power house linked by a two arch bridge, largely unaltered.

locations.name: Dalesice Brewery
locations.setting: Small joint stock brewery in the village of Dalesice with 19th century brewhouse machinery, a malting floor, an on site hotel and restaurant, and a brewery museum.

locations.name: DEPO2015
locations.setting: Former bus depot in Plzeň converted into a creative and cultural centre, with workshop halls, a gallery and event space that keep the building's industrial steel roof trusses.
locations.facilities: Industrial complex with a cafe, market hall and event spaces; wheelchair accessible throughout except some office areas (own site).
locations.logistics: On-site parking within the complex; address Presslova 14, Plzen (own site).

locations.name: Dlouhe Strane Power Plant
locations.region: Olomouc Region (Loucna nad Desnou, Jeseniky mountains)
locations.setting: Pumped storage hydroelectric plant in the Jeseniky mountains with an upper reservoir on a bare ridge and a turbine hall built deep inside the mountain, open for guided tours.

locations.name: Dolní Morava Sky Bridge
locations.setting: 721-metre pedestrian suspension bridge strung between two ridges above the Dolní Morava mountain resort near Králický Sněžník, with a glass-floored lookout and a nearby forest canopy walkway.

locations.name: Dolní Vítkovice
locations.setting: Former ironworks and coking plant just south of Ostrava's centre, with blast furnaces, a gasometer and a coal tower preserved as an industrial heritage site with exhibition and event space.
locations.suitability: Photography and filming on site is governed by the venue's published rules for photography and filming in the area and its buildings (own site).

locations.name: Flaje Dam
locations.region: Usti nad Labem Region (Cesky Jiretin, Krusne hory)
locations.setting: Concrete arch dam in the Krusne hory mountains near the German border, holding back a reservoir in a forested valley, with the dam wall and spillway accessible on foot.

locations.name: Gong
locations.setting: Former gasometer at the Lower Vítkovice ironworks in Ostrava converted into a circular concert and exhibition hall inside its riveted steel shell.

locations.name: Grandhotel Pupp
locations.setting: Baroque and neoclassical spa hotel at the head of Karlovy Vary's colonnade, with ballrooms, a casino and period guest rooms dating back to the 18th century.
locations.facilities: Festive Hall: 735 sqm, ceiling height 15 m, natural light, up to 500 people (cocktail), 424 (banquet), 400 (theatre). Johann Georg hall: 122 sqm, up to 84 (theatre), 70 (cocktail). Heinrich room: 32 sqm, up to 12 (block setup). Beethoven rooms: 29 to 73 sqm, 8 to 45 (theatre), combined Beethoven II+III up to 50 (cocktail). Floor loading capacity is described as sufficient for passenger cars (own site).
locations.suitability: The hotel says it has attracted filmmakers since the early days of cinema, with dozens of films shot there including the Bond film Casino Royale (own site).

locations.name: Holešovice Market
locations.setting: Late 19th century cattle market and slaughterhouse complex on the Vltava embankment in Holešovice, with brick market halls now used for food stalls, shops and events.
locations.facilities: Hala 13: 1,500 sqm. Hala 11: 560 sqm. Hala 17: 900 sqm. Trzni namesti (market square): 2,600 sqm. Korzo: 4,000 sqm. Hala 40 (4th floor): 485 sqm. Hala 22 market stalls from 10 sqm (own site).

locations.name: Hotel Jalta
locations.setting: 1958 socialist-modernist hotel on Wenceslas Square with a preserved Cold War-era nuclear bunker in the basement, run today as a functioning hotel with a small museum.

locations.name: Hotel Thermal
locations.setting: Brutalist 1970s hotel and congress complex beside the Ohře river in Karlovy Vary, with a rooftop pool and an open-air cinema terrace, the home base of the city's international film festival.

locations.name: Hranicar
locations.region: Usti nad Labem Region (Usti nad Labem)
locations.setting: Former border crossing customs house on the Elbe riverbank, converted into a community arts centre with a cinema, gallery, bar and courtyard used for events.

locations.name: Jested Tower Hotel
locations.setting: Single cone shaped hotel and television transmitter on the summit of Jested mountain above Liberec, reached by cable car, with a circular restaurant and panoramic windows.

locations.name: Jihoceske Divadlo (South Bohemian Theatre)
locations.setting: Repertory theatre in central Ceske Budejovice with an early 20th century auditorium, stage house and backstage workshops still used for daily opera, drama and ballet productions.

locations.name: Klasterni Hradisko (Military Hospital Olomouc)
locations.setting: Former Premonstratensian monastery on the edge of Olomouc, now a working military hospital, with baroque courtyards and church interiors alongside functioning medical wards.

locations.name: Klementinum
locations.setting: Former Jesuit college in Prague's Old Town now housing the National Library, with a baroque astronomical tower, mirrored chapel and historic library halls available for events and filming.

locations.name: Landek Park
locations.setting: Former hard coal mine at Petrkovice on the edge of Ostrava, now an open-air mining museum with pit head towers, wagons and underground galleries open to visitors.

locations.name: Lovosice Port
locations.setting: River port and container terminal on the Elbe at Lovosice in north Bohemia, with cranes, quaysides and warehouse sheds serving inland barge traffic.

locations.name: Lucerna Palace
locations.setting: 1921 Art Nouveau passage complex in central Prague, with a domed concert hall, one of the city's oldest cinemas and a chain of shopping arcades under glass roofs.
locations.facilities: Main cinema: 453 seats, 4K digital projection with 3D and Dolby Surround 7.1. Small cinema hall: 51 seats, 2K digital projection with 3D and Dolby Surround 7.1. Marble Hall: 300 sqm, 150 to 350 people depending on the event, parquet floor, stage, dressing room and toilets. Gallery: 400 sqm, 150 to 200 people. Cafe: 300 sqm, 120 seats. Club Konicek: 90 sqm, 44 seats (own site).

locations.name: Luhačovice Spa
locations.setting: Moravian spa town built up from 1902 around mineral springs, with colonnades and hotel buildings designed by architect Dušan Jurkovič in a distinctive folk-art style.

locations.name: Mahen Theatre
locations.setting: 1882 neo-baroque theatre in Brno, the first public building in Europe lit entirely by Edison electric light, still in use as part of the National Theatre Brno.
locations.known_for: First electrically lit theatre building in Europe (1882)

locations.name: Masaryk University
locations.setting: Brno's largest university, spanning a historic main building near the city centre and modern faculty campuses, with lecture halls and campus architecture listed by the film commission.

photo.author: Kounics_palace_in_Brno_2010.jpg: User:Sveter (Please credit as "Petr Šmerkl, Wikipedia" in case you use this outside WMF

locations.name: Michal Mine
locations.setting: Complete early 20th century coal mine surface plant in Ostrava-Michálkovice, with preserved machine hall, boiler house and pithead baths run as a branch of the National Technical Museum.
locations.suitability: Exterior photography is permitted for personal use. Interior photography without flash, tripod, selfie stick or lighting equipment is allowed only in guide-designated rooms for personal use. Guided-tour filming and drone footage are not permitted (own site).
locations.logistics: Parking in front of the mine entrance; buses park within the grounds (own site).

locations.name: Municipal House
locations.setting: Art Nouveau civic building on Republic Square in Prague completed in 1912, with the Smetana concert hall, ceremonial reception rooms, a café and restaurant behind an ornate mosaic facade.
locations.facilities: Ten halls and rooms including the Smetana Hall, Mayor's Hall, Gregr Hall, Sladkovsky Hall, Palacky Hall and Rieger Hall, plus several parlours and a confectionery space (own site).
locations.logistics: Address nam. Republiky 1090/5, Prague 1. Metro A (Mustek, 4 minute walk) or metro B (Namesti Republiky); tram lines 6, 8, 15, 26 to Namesti Republiky (own site).

locations.name: Olomouc Town Hall
locations.setting: Gothic and Renaissance town hall on Olomouc's main square, with a tower, an open loggia and an astronomical clock rebuilt in a socialist-realist style after wartime damage.

locations.name: Pardubice Hospital
locations.setting: Regional hospital campus in Pardubice combining older pavilion wings with newer clinical buildings, listed by the national film commission as an available filming location.

locations.name: Prague Main Railway Station
locations.setting: Prague's principal railway terminus, with an Art Nouveau departure hall from 1909 by architect Josef Fanta grafted onto a modern underground concourse and platforms.

locations.name: Prague Metro
locations.setting: Three line underground network opened in 1974, with deep late-communist era stations finished in coloured anodised aluminium panels and marble, still in daily operation.

photo.author: Matěj Čadil=en:User:Neral as confirmed here 2007-01-25 (in Czech)

locations.name: Secondary School of Textile Engineering Liberec
locations.setting: Working textile college on Textilni street with period spinning and weaving machinery still in place alongside plain classroom interiors and a gated parking yard.

locations.name: Sokol Hradec Králové Sports Complex
locations.setting: Functionalist gymnasium and sports hall complex built for the Sokol movement in Hradec Králové, with large open exercise halls and period fittings.

locations.name: Techmania Science Center
locations.setting: Interactive science museum in a former Skoda Works foundry hall in the Bory district of Plzen, combining a large industrial shed with modern exhibition halls and a planetarium.

locations.name: Terezín Small Fortress
locations.setting: 18th century star fort east of Terezín used as a political prison under Austria-Hungary and as a Gestapo prison during the German occupation, with cell blocks and courtyards preserved as a memorial.

locations.name: The Papirna Multifunctional Center
locations.setting: Renovated paper mill building of about 4,000 square metres by the Radbuza river near central Plzen, holding a large industrial hall, an art studio, cafe and exhibition rooms.

locations.name: Thomas Bata Villa
locations.setting: Functionalist 1911 villa built for shoe manufacturer Tomáš Baťa on the edge of Zlín's factory district, later enlarged and now used as a museum of the Baťa family and its management methods.

locations.name: Tomas Bata University in Zlín
locations.setting: University built inside the former Baťa shoe factory's functionalist halls in Zlín, glass-and-steel-frame factory buildings from the 1930s adapted into lecture rooms and laboratories.

locations.name: Underground Water Reservoir Brno
locations.setting: Disused 19th century brick water reservoir cut into a hillside near Brno's exhibition grounds, with vaulted underground chambers now hired out for exhibitions and events.
locations.facilities: Vaulted underground spaces; declared a cultural monument in 2019 (Czech Film Commission).
locations.logistics: Owned by the City of Brno; administration is being handed to TIC BRNO (Brno Tourist Information Centre), which leases the space to film crews (Czech Film Commission).

locations.name: Villa Stiassni
locations.setting: 1929 functionalist villa in Brno built for textile manufacturer Alfred Stiassni and later used as a state guesthouse, with period furniture, gardens and a swimming pool.
locations.facilities: Garden of over 3 hectares with a tennis court, swimming pool, terrace and loggia. Interior salons with wood panelling, marble fireplaces and stucco. A modern lecture building is also on site (current official site: vila-stiassni.cz).
locations.logistics: Parking on Hroznova street, not within the villa grounds. Address Hroznova 14, Brno-Pisarky (vila-stiassni.cz).

locations.name: Villa Tugendhat
locations.setting: UNESCO-listed 1930 modernist villa in Brno by Ludwig Mies van der Rohe, with a glass-walled living hall, an onyx wall and a travertine terrace over the garden and city.
locations.facilities: Garden and multiple floors, including exhibition rooms on the technical floor (own site).
locations.suitability: Filming and photo shoots are listed among the event types permitted at the villa (own site).

locations.name: Winternitz Villa
locations.setting: 1932 house in Prague's Smíchov district designed by Adolf Loos around his raumplan of interlocking split levels, now a museum open for tours and filming by appointment.

locations.name: Zlín Factory Complex
locations.setting: Grid of red brick functionalist factory halls built by the Baťa shoe company in Zlín from the 1920s, now reused as a university, offices and cultural venues.

locations.name: Bornholm Airport
locations.setting: Regional airport near Roenne on Bornholm with scheduled flights to Copenhagen, Aalborg, Billund and Sonderborg, the island's only air link.

locations.name: Carlsberg Byen
locations.setting: Former Carlsberg brewery grounds in Copenhagen, redeveloped into a city district that keeps historic brewery halls and towers alongside new office, retail and residential buildings.

locations.name: Christiansborg Palace
locations.setting: Government palace on the Slotsholmen islet housing the Danish Parliament, Prime Minister's Office and Supreme Court, with a riding ground complex and palace square.
locations.suitability: The palace's manager, the Royal Danish Collection, states it welcomes press inquiries, including for TV shows, and that holders of valid press credentials get free admission to any of its palaces without advance booking (contact via the Head of Communications).

locations.name: CopenHill (Amager Bakke)
locations.setting: Working waste-to-energy plant in Copenhagen with a rooftop ski slope, climbing wall and hiking trail built onto its sloped roof, plus a rooftop bar and cafe.
locations.facilities: Rooftop bar and event space, cafe, elevator access to the roof

locations.name: Dokk1
locations.setting: A large glass and concrete public library and citizen service building on Aarhus harbourfront, with open multi-storey interiors and a public square outside.

locations.name: DR Koncerthuset
locations.setting: Concert hall in Copenhagen's Orestad district built for Danish public broadcaster DR, with a main concert hall, four recording studios and a restaurant, available for external hire.
locations.facilities: Concert hall, four recording studios, external hire for concerts and conferences

locations.name: FAENGSLET (Horsens State Prison)
locations.setting: Former Danish state prison in Horsens, closed in 2006 and reopened as a prison museum whose cell wings, exercise yards and workshop buildings are hired out for events and overnight stays.
locations.facilities: Cell wings, museum halls, conference and event spaces, overnight accommodation

locations.name: Filmby Aarhus
locations.setting: Creative business park in Aarhus's Sydhavnen district housing over 80 film, TV, gaming and animation companies, with production premises and an event bar for hire.
locations.facilities: Rental of commercial premises and production facilities, event bar

locations.name: Gammel Estrup
locations.setting: Renaissance manor house in Jutland, home to Denmark's national museum of manor life, with period rooms, stables, a moat and surrounding parkland used for events.

locations.name: H.C. Andersens Hus
locations.setting: A museum in Odense's old town dedicated to Hans Christian Andersen, combining a modern underground exhibition building with the historic house and courtyard where he was born.

locations.name: Hotel Koldingfjord
locations.setting: A former sanatorium turned hotel and conference centre on the shore of Kolding Fjord, with period interiors, function rooms and parkland running down to the water.

photo.author: FaceMePLS from The Hague, The Netherlands

locations.name: Kronborg Castle
locations.setting: Renaissance fortress at the narrowest point of the Øresund strait, with ramparts, a large courtyard and vaulted casemates, known as the Elsinore of Shakespeare's Hamlet.

locations.name: Moens Klint (GeoCenter)
locations.setting: White chalk cliffs on the island of Moen rising up to 128 metres above the Baltic Sea, with a science centre, forest trails and beach access at the cliff base.
locations.suitability: Group bookings, guided tours and business/school event hosting

locations.name: Nordisk Film Studios
locations.setting: Working studio lot in Valby founded in 1906, the world's oldest continuously active film studio, with shooting stages, post-production facilities and a 360-degree LED stage.
locations.facilities: 360-degree LED stage of 16 m diameter and 5.5 m height with LED walls and ceiling and an optional LED floor (ROE panels, up to 6,000 nits), run by Nordisk Film Shortcut; dressing rooms, makeup facilities and large parking for crew and grip trucks.
locations.suitability: The LED stage is offered for films, series, commercials, music videos and live events with virtual production supervision, Unreal Engine content, previs and driving plates; it takes vehicles, boats and planes up to 15 m. The stage runs on solar power from 2023.
locations.logistics: Mosedalvej 14, 2500 Valby, on the Nordisk Film lot; large parking for crew and grip trucks.

locations.name: Nordkraft
locations.setting: Former coal-fired power station on Aalborg's harbour front converted into a culture house, with theatre, music and exhibition halls inside the original turbine building.
locations.price_note: Commercial photography in shared areas from DKK 1,000 (about EUR 134) per day (own site)

locations.name: Odense Havn
locations.setting: Commercial port on Funen with 3.9 kilometres of quay, heavy-lift cranes and large storage areas, used for offshore wind component handling and industrial tenants.
locations.facilities: Industrial space and quay for lease, heavy-load area, crane operations up to 1,200 tonnes

locations.name: Refshaleøen
locations.setting: Former B&W shipyard peninsula in Copenhagen harbour, its industrial sheds, open dock space and workshop halls now let out for events, studios and small businesses.
locations.facilities: Industrial halls, open quay and dock space, event venues for hire

locations.name: Roskilde Cathedral
locations.setting: Brick cathedral in Roskilde and UNESCO World Heritage site, burial church of the Danish monarchy for over 500 years, with regular organ concerts and cultural events.

photo.author: CucombreLibre from New York, NY, USA

locations.name: Tivoli Gardens
locations.setting: Amusement park and pleasure garden in central Copenhagen dating from 1843, with rides, concert stages, themed architecture and landscaped gardens.
locations.facilities: Event and meeting spaces named on the business site include Nimb, Axelborgsalen and Kilden i Haven.

locations.name: Torvehallerne
locations.setting: Two glass-roofed market halls in central Copenhagen with food and drink stalls under one enclosed roof, plus an adjoining public square outside for exterior coverage.

locations.name: Utzon Center
locations.setting: Waterfront exhibition and knowledge centre in Aalborg designed by architect Jorn Utzon as his last work, with gallery halls, a restaurant and rooms available for hire.
locations.facilities: Room hire and booking, on-site restaurant

locations.name: Cable Factory (Kaapelitehdas)
locations.setting: Former Nokia cable factory in Helsinki's Ruoholahti district, a long brick industrial building with high factory halls, now a large cultural centre housing museums, studios, galleries and rentable event spaces.
locations.facilities: Dedicated space-for-rent pages for event and studio hire within the former factory halls.
locations.logistics: Managed by Kiinteistö Oy Kaapelitalo; member of the Trans Europe Halles network of industrial cultural venues.

locations.name: Finlayson Area
locations.setting: Former cotton mill founded in 1820 beside the Tammerkoski rapids in Tampere, a complex of red-brick factory buildings including the 1877 Plevna weaving hall, now holding restaurants, a cinema, shops and offices.
locations.facilities: About 80,000 sq m of rentable space across the former factory buildings; individual premises range from about 10 sq m to several thousand sq m. The buildings hold the BREEAM In-Use environmental certificate.

locations.name: Helsinki Olympic Stadium
locations.setting: Functionalist 1938 stadium built for the 1952 Olympics, with a 72-metre tower and a renovated bowl used today for athletics, concerts, conferences and stadium tours.
locations.facilities: Meeting rooms, restaurant, seated event spaces and a rentable tower with panoramic views.

locations.name: Ivalo
locations.setting: Village on the Ivalo River about 250 kilometres north of the Arctic Circle, surrounded by boreal forest and fells, with deep snow and polar night for much of the year.

locations.name: Kehräsaari
locations.setting: Former needle factory and wool mill on a small island in central Tampere, its 1897 red-brick U-shaped building now a shopping and business centre linked by footbridge to the riverside Koskikeskus district.
locations.facilities: Former needle factory and spinning mill, now used as a commercial and business centre between Laukontori marketplace and Koskikeskus shopping centre.
locations.logistics: 0.5 km from Tampere Central Square.

locations.name: Levi Ski Resort
locations.setting: Finland's largest ski resort on Levi fell in Kittila, with 43 marked slopes and 27 lifts amid birch and pine wilderness, used in winter for skiing and Northern Lights and in summer for fell hiking under the midnight sun.
locations.known_for: The Grand Tour: A Scandi Flick (2022)

locations.name: Mediapolis
locations.setting: Media campus at broadcaster Yle's Tohloppi site in Tampere, with fully equipped television studios and a 1,500 square metre factory hall stage available for hire.
locations.facilities: Two Yle broadcast studios of 432 m2 (24 x 18 m) and 342 m2 (19 x 18 m) with tungsten lighting, hoists and 360-degree curtains; a 1,200 m2 Factory Hall (26 x 54.5 m, 10 m clear height); smaller TAMK and United studios of 133 and 198 m2; wardrobe and makeup rooms, six sound studios and edit stations.
locations.suitability: Studios are booked through a named contact per facility; the campus also offers production services, catering, event spaces and office facilities.
locations.logistics: 32,000 m2 campus in the Tohloppi district of Tampere where 1,000 to 1,100 people work and study daily

locations.name: Melo Power Plant
locations.setting: A hydroelectric power plant in Nokia near Tampere offering both industrial interiors and surrounding nature for productions, listed by Film Tampere as a filming location.
locations.logistics: Located at Melontie 59, 37140 Nokia, about 20 km from Tampere's central square

locations.name: Parking Garages by Finnpark
locations.setting: A network of multi storey car parks operated by Finnpark in and around central Tampere, listed by Film Tampere as available filming locations.

locations.name: Pitkäniemi Hospital Area
locations.setting: Former psychiatric hospital on a lakeshore park in Nokia near Tampere, with stone buildings from the 1890s including an Italianate villa, in clinical use from 1900 until closure in 2024 and now largely vacant.
locations.facilities: Historical stone hospital buildings completed in 1894-1895 in parkland on the shore of Lake Pyhäjärvi, part of Tampere University Hospital. The former chief's residence ('the Castle') has Italian Renaissance-style columned terraces and now houses the Pitkäniemi Hospital Museum.
locations.logistics: 12.5 km from Tampere Central Square.

locations.name: Senate Square
locations.setting: Neoclassical square by Carl Ludvig Engel framed by Helsinki Cathedral, the Government Palace and the university, long used as a stand-in for imperial St Petersburg and Soviet-era Moscow.

locations.name: Sibelius Hall
locations.setting: A wooden concert hall on the shore of Lake Vesijarvi in Lahti, with a main hall, several conference rooms and a live music club, offering full event production and streaming services.
locations.facilities: Main hall (Paasali), Metsahalli, Puusepan Sali, conference rooms, restaurants and the Finlandia-klubi live music venue
locations.logistics: Located at Ankkurikatu 7, Lahti

locations.name: Stable Yards (Tallipiha)
locations.setting: A 19th century stable courtyard from the Finlayson factory community in Tampere, restored with Russian style cottages that now house craft shops and a cafe, listed by Film Tampere as a filming location.
locations.logistics: Located at Kuninkaankatu 4, about 0.7 km from Tampere's central square

locations.name: Suomenlinna
locations.setting: Sea fortress built from 1748 across a cluster of islands off Helsinki, with stone bastions, tunnels, dry docks and cobbled courtyards, now a UNESCO World Heritage site with museums and open parkland.
locations.logistics: Official site publishes separate instructions for filming and photography and a dedicated contact for bookings.

locations.name: Suvilahti
locations.setting: Former power plant and gasworks complex in Helsinki with red-brick industrial halls and open concrete yards, now a cultural venue mixing galleries, restaurants and a brewery inside the original industrial shells.
locations.facilities: Site explicitly offers outdoor and indoor space rental for events, festivals and photo shoots.
locations.logistics: Managed by Kiinteistö Oy Kaapelitalo; multiple independent tenants occupy separate buildings on the site.

locations.name: Tampere City Hall
locations.setting: A neo renaissance city hall from 1890 on Tampere's central square, with several period halls, listed by Film Tampere as a filming location.
locations.logistics: Located at Keskustori 10, at the edge of Tampere's central square

locations.name: Tampere Hall
locations.setting: Largest congress centre in the Nordic countries, a modern building beside Sorsapuisto park in central Tampere with a 1,756-seat main auditorium and several smaller halls used for concerts and conferences.

locations.name: Tampere Market Hall (Kauppahalli)
locations.setting: Largest market hall in the Nordic countries when it opened in 1901, a protected two-story brick building in central Tampere with roughly 30 food stalls, cafes and restaurants.

locations.name: Tullikamari
locations.setting: A former customs warehouse in Tampere converted into a cultural venue with a large main hall and a smaller club space, used for concerts, theatre and festivals, listed by Film Tampere as a filming location.
locations.logistics: Located at Tullikamarin aukio 2, about 1 km from Tampere's central square

locations.name: Turku Castle
locations.setting: Medieval keep begun around 1280 at the mouth of the Aura river, expanded into a Renaissance bailey under Gustav Vasa in the 16th century, now a city museum with period rooms, banqueting halls and rentable event spaces.
locations.known_for: Sadan miekan mies (1951), The Girl King (2015)
locations.facilities: Rooms published for hire: Kuninkaan sali (King's Hall, up to 250), Linnan kirkko (Castle Church, up to 240), Kuningattaren sali (Queen's Hall, up to 180), Bryggman-sali (up to 120 for lectures, 80 for banquets), Eteläinen sali (Southern Hall, up to 100), Kuningattaren kamari (Queen's Chamber, up to 50), Herrainkellari (Gentlemen's Cellar, up to 30), plus courtyard areas.

photo.author: Markus Koljonen (Dilaudid) with thanks to Jontts and Turku Cathedral

locations.name: Abbaye Royale de Fontevraud
locations.setting: Former royal abbey near Chinon founded in 1101, with a Romanesque church, medieval kitchens and cloisters plus an on-site hotel, its own site publishing information for film and TV shoots.

locations.name: Accor Arena
locations.setting: Multi-purpose indoor arena in Bercy seating up to about 20,300, built into a grass-covered pyramid, used for concerts, sport and large events.

locations.name: Aeroport Paris-Charles de Gaulle
locations.setting: France's main international airport north of Paris, with terminals, control-tower views and airside areas that operator Groupe ADP makes available for filming through a dedicated production service.

locations.name: Allianz Riviera
locations.setting: Nice football stadium with a translucent wave-shaped roof, home to OGC Nice and used for concerts and other large events.

locations.name: Aquaboulevard
locations.setting: Indoor and outdoor water park in the 15th arrondissement, with wave pools, slides and tropical-style planting, hired through its own professional booking service for shoots and events.

locations.name: Arenes de Nimes
locations.setting: Roman amphitheatre built around 100 AD in the centre of Nimes, seating up to 24,000 for its own ferias and concerts, with a covered arena floor usable for filming outside the events calendar.

locations.name: Base sous-marine de Saint-Nazaire (La Base)
locations.setting: Reinforced-concrete U-boat pens built by the German navy in WWII on the Saint-Nazaire docks, now holding exhibition halls, a climbing wall and a rooftop garden.

locations.name: Bassins de Lumières
locations.setting: Former WWII submarine pens on the Bordeaux docks converted into a digital art centre, with four raw concrete basins used for large-scale wall and floor projections.
locations.facilities: Two indoor spaces: the Citerne (155 sqm, 360-degree projection) and the Cube (220 sqm, soundproofed), plus elevated walkways and tiered seating. Overall capacity ranges from 50 to 900 for a cocktail reception or 50 to 700 for a seated dinner.
locations.suitability: The venue lists professional events as one of five event categories it hosts, alongside cocktails, seated dinners, and private visits.

locations.name: Bibliothèque nationale de France, site Richelieu
locations.setting: Historic national library building in central Paris with a 19th-century domed reading room and ornate galleries, reopened after a long restoration.
locations.facilities: At the Richelieu site, the Salle Ovale seats up to 220 for a dinner or holds up to 300 for a cocktail reception. Other hireable spaces are the Hall Vivienne, the Vivienne garden, and the Salon d'Honneur.
locations.suitability: Filming and photography require prior written authorization from BnF, covering the Richelieu, François-Mitterrand, Arsenal, Opéra and CTBnF sites; an exception applies only to images made for strictly private, non-commercial use.
locations.logistics: Richelieu site spaces can be hired from 6pm Wednesday to Sunday, and all day on Monday when the site is closed to the public.

locations.name: Bourse de Commerce, Pinault Collection
locations.setting: Former 19th-century grain exchange with a circular rotunda and glass dome, renovated by Tadao Ando with an internal concrete cylinder as a contemporary art museum.
locations.facilities: Ground-floor Salon and Passage (up to 800 for a cocktail reception or 220 for a seated dinner), Foyer on floor -1 (up to 300 for a cocktail reception), a semi-circular Auditorium (284 seats), the Petit Salon (up to 70 people), and the restaurant La Halle aux Grains (125 for a cocktail reception or 100 for a dinner).
locations.logistics: Private events run Monday to Thursday from 8:30-10:30am and from 7:30pm, and from 7pm on Tuesdays when the museum is closed to the public.

locations.name: Cap Sciences
locations.setting: Science centre inside Hangar 20, a former dockside cargo warehouse on the Garonne in Bordeaux, keeping the hangar's steel roof trusses over its exhibition floor, with halls listed to hire.

locations.name: Centre Historique Minier (Lewarde Mining Centre)
locations.setting: Preserved coal mine museum in the former Delloye colliery, with pithead buildings, a headframe, underground galleries and workshops from the Nord-Pas-de-Calais coalfield.
locations.price_note: Meeting room hire from EUR 145 per half day (34-36 sqm rooms) up to EUR 1,000 per full day for the Auditorium Georges Delerue; technical support is a mandatory extra at EUR 35 per hour (own site, 2026 rates)
locations.facilities: Salle Jules Mousseron (70 sqm), Salle Lucien Jonas (36 sqm) and Salle Albert Bouquillon (34 sqm) meeting rooms, plus the Auditorium Georges Delerue (200 seats: 175 armchairs with a writing tablet, 22 folding seats and 3 wheelchair spaces, with a 45 sqm stage, a 4x3m screen and an audio system). Wheelchair accessible by lift.

locations.name: Chamonix-Mont-Blanc
locations.setting: Alpine resort town below Mont Blanc with cable cars up to the Aiguille du Midi and nearby glaciers, a base for mountaineering and skiing since the 19th century.

locations.name: Château d'If
locations.setting: 16th-century island fortress off Marseille used as a state prison into the 19th century, the setting of The Count of Monte Cristo and a location in The French Connection.
locations.facilities: 1,547 sqm of castle interior with several small rooms, 600 sqm of terraces, and a 1,700 sqm parade ground. The castle interior and terraces each hold up to 100 people standing; the parade ground holds up to 500 standing.
locations.suitability: Both interior and exterior filming are offered year-round, for films, series, documentaries and advertisements.

locations.name: Chateau l'Hospitalet
locations.setting: Wine estate on the La Clape massif near Narbonne, with vineyards, cellars, a hotel and restaurants around a courtyard, hosting its own annual jazz festival and grounds used for private events.

locations.name: Chateau La Coste
locations.setting: Organic vineyard estate near Aix-en-Provence with a sculpture trail and pavilions by architects including Tadao Ando and Renzo Piano, a hotel and restaurant, and grounds hired for weddings.

locations.name: Chemin de Fer de la Baie de Somme
locations.setting: Heritage steam and diesel railway running along the Somme bay between Le Crotoy, Saint-Valery-sur-Somme and Cayeux, with period stations and rolling stock.
locations.price_note: Private train charter from EUR 2,200 including tax for the Belle Époque steam train (March to September) or EUR 2,500 including tax for the 4 Saisons diesel train (October to February), plus meals at EUR 43 per adult and EUR 20 per child under 12 (own site, 2026 rates)
locations.facilities: Two heritage trains available for private charter: Belle Époque (steam, seats up to 115) and 4 Saisons (diesel, seats up to 96). Neither train is wheelchair accessible or pet-friendly.
locations.logistics: Lunch charter departs Saint-Valery at 12:00 with a meal stop on the sea wall from 12:10 to 14:15, returning at 15:20. Dinner charter departs the Saint-Valery Canal depot at 19:00, returning around 23:00-23:20. Booking requires a signed quote and a EUR 1,000 deposit, with the balance due 15 days before by bank cheque; no refund for late arrival or no-show.

locations.name: Cite de l'Automobile
locations.setting: Mulhouse car museum built around the Schlumpf brothers' collection, with several hundred vehicles under one roof lit by rows of replica cast-iron lamp posts, its site publishing venue-hire terms.

locations.name: Cite de l'Espace
locations.setting: Space-themed science centre on the eastern edge of Toulouse, with a full-size Ariane rocket outdoors, planetarium domes and simulator halls, hired out for seminars and corporate events.

locations.name: Cite de la Mer
locations.setting: Maritime museum inside Cherbourg's 1933 Art Deco former transatlantic liner terminal, keeping the original departure hall, with a decommissioned submarine on display and dockside harbour views.

locations.name: Cité de la Mode et du Design
locations.setting: Former riverside customs warehouse on the Seine reclad in a green glass and steel skin, housing a design school, offices, a club and event floors over the water.

locations.name: Cité de la Voile Éric Tabarly (Keroman submarine base)
locations.setting: WWII U-boat pens on the Keroman peninsula in Lorient with roofs up to 7.5 metres thick, now holding a sailing museum, boatyards and a marina business park.
locations.facilities: Named spaces include the Auditorium, Karré Affaires (modular cocktail/reception space), two equipped meeting rooms, a permanent exhibition space, and Hall Pen Duick (modular for conferences, cocktails and exhibitions). Overall capacity ranges from 20 to 380 people. Equipped with tables, chairs, flipcharts, video projectors, UHD screens, sound systems, microphones and wifi.
locations.logistics: In Lorient, Brittany; about 3 hours from Paris by train, with Lorient station 10 minutes away. Pricing is by quotation only.

locations.name: Cité des Sciences et de l'Industrie
locations.setting: Large science museum in the Parc de la Villette built inside a converted 1960s abattoir hall, with the geodesic dome cinema La Géode standing alongside it.

locations.name: Cité du Cinéma (Studios de Paris)
locations.setting: Studio campus in a converted riverside power station with sound stages, workshops and offices around a monumental glass-roofed nave.
locations.known_for: Lucy, Valerian and the City of a Thousand Planets
locations.facilities: Nine sound stages from 6,506 to 22,271 sq ft (largest Stage 5, 201 x 111 ft, about 2,070 m2) with 47 to 52.5 ft to the grid; offices, artist green rooms with hair and makeup, VIP green rooms, workshops and storage.
locations.suitability: Stages offered with adjoining offices, green rooms, workshops and storage inside the Cite du Cinema campus; the site keeps a list of productions shot there.
locations.logistics: 20 rue Ampere, Saint-Denis: 30 minutes from Charles de Gaulle airport, 20 minutes from Le Bourget, 30 to 40 minutes from central Paris; served by RER D and metro lines 13 and 14 (direct to Orly), A86 and A1 motorway access, two four-star hotels a five-minute walk away.

locations.name: Cite du Livre
locations.setting: Former match factory in Aix-en-Provence, converted into a library and performance complex that keeps its industrial brick shell and a large auditorium used by the Festival d'Aix.

locations.name: Cite du Train
locations.setting: One of the world's largest railway museums, in Mulhouse, with locomotives and carriages under a long-span roof and a reconstructed period station platform, published as available for hire and filming.

locations.name: Cité Frugès
locations.setting: Estate of concrete houses built by Le Corbusier and Pierre Jeanneret in Pessac in 1926 in flat-roofed cubic and terraced forms, UNESCO-listed since 2016.

locations.name: Cité Internationale Universitaire de Paris
locations.setting: Campus of more than 40 national residence halls in varied architectural styles on the southern edge of Paris, housing international students since the 1920s.
locations.facilities: 34-hectare campus with 47 architecturally varied buildings dating from 1925 onward, offered for professional events as well as filming; parking for trucks and production equipment is positioned close to the sets, with a dedicated on-site team supporting productions.
locations.suitability: Described by CIUP as France's first multi-set filming location, with both interior settings (art deco lounges, halls, corridors, staircases, offices) and exterior settings (building facades, landscaped grounds). States that no prefectural authorization is required to film there; more than 500 productions have shot there in 10 years.

locations.name: Cité Radieuse, Marseille
locations.setting: Le Corbusier's 1952 concrete apartment block on stilts in Marseille, with 337 duplex units, an internal shopping street and a rooftop terrace.

locations.name: Écomusée Creusot Montceau
locations.setting: Industrial heritage network around the former Schneider steelworks in Le Creusot, with the Château de la Verrerie glassworks-turned-mansion as its main site.

locations.name: Étretat Cliffs
locations.setting: White chalk cliffs with natural arches and a freestanding needle rising above a pebble beach on the Alabaster Coast.

locations.name: Futuroscope
locations.setting: Multimedia theme park north of Poitiers built around futuristic pavilions and a lake, with cinema domes and landscaped outdoor sets, offering seminar and private event hire outside opening hours.

locations.name: Gare Saint Sauveur
locations.setting: Former goods yard of a 19th-century Lille railway station, now an exhibition and events venue keeping the open shed structure and platform-level halls of the original depot.

locations.name: Grand Port Maritime de Marseille
locations.setting: France's largest port, with the working container terminals and warehouses of Marseille-Fos and the historic Joliette basin, with its own published filming-permit process for productions.

locations.name: Haras National de Lamballe
locations.setting: State stud farm founded in 1825 in a former army barracks in Lamballe, with stone stable blocks around a courtyard and a riding arena, its own site listing hire for weddings and seminars.

locations.name: Haras National du Pin
locations.setting: France's oldest national stud, an 18th-century complex of stables around a formal chateau-style courtyard in the Orne countryside, with an equestrian arena and grounds listed for seminar hire.

locations.name: Hôpital Bicêtre
locations.setting: Large hospital complex south of Paris with historic pavilions and a tall water reservoir building, listed by AP-HP among the sites it regularly opens to film crews.
locations.suitability: All filming at AP-HP hospitals is subject to prior authorization; arrangements must respect the image rights of patients, staff and visitors as well as hospital regulations. Filming gives rise to a fee for occupying public domain space, based on an internal AP-HP tariff scale that is not published online.

locations.name: Hôpital Maritime de Berck
locations.setting: Seafront AP-HP hospital in Berck-sur-Mer built as a 19th-century marine sanatorium, named on the AP-HP's list of hospitals that regularly welcome film shoots.
locations.suitability: All filming at AP-HP hospitals is subject to prior authorization; arrangements must respect the image rights of patients, staff and visitors as well as hospital regulations. Filming gives rise to a fee for occupying public domain space, based on an internal AP-HP tariff scale that is not published online.

locations.name: Hôpital Raymond-Poincaré
locations.setting: Rehabilitation hospital in Garches with early 20th-century pavilion wards and gardens, one of the AP-HP sites named as regularly opened for commercial filming.
locations.suitability: All filming at AP-HP hospitals is subject to prior authorization; arrangements must respect the image rights of patients, staff and visitors as well as hospital regulations. Filming gives rise to a fee for occupying public domain space, based on an internal AP-HP tariff scale that is not published online.

locations.name: Hôpital Saint-Louis
locations.setting: Working Paris hospital built around an early 17th-century brick and stone quadrilateral courtyard, one of the AP-HP sites named as regularly hosting commercial filming.
locations.suitability: All filming at AP-HP hospitals is subject to prior authorization; arrangements must respect the image rights of patients, staff and visitors as well as hospital regulations. Filming gives rise to a fee for occupying public domain space, based on an internal AP-HP tariff scale that is not published online.

locations.name: Institut Lumière
locations.setting: Museum in the former Lumière family home in Lyon, dedicated to Auguste and Louis Lumière and the birth of cinema, close to the site of their original factory.
locations.facilities: Hangar du Premier-Film: 300 sqm, seats 220 for a dinner or 300 for a cocktail reception, plus an adjoining cinema seating 269 (with 8 wheelchair spaces), 3 plasma screens, 2 x 35mm projectors and 1 digital projector. Jardin d'Hiver at Villa Lumière: 60 sqm, 35 seated or 70 for a cocktail reception. Villa Lumière also has two screening rooms in the basement.
