locations.known_for: Adriano Olivetti: La forza di un sogno (2013 miniseries)

locations.name: Lingotto Rooftop Track and Pinacoteca Agnelli
locations.setting: Former Fiat car factory in Turin with a rooftop test track encircling the building, now containing exhibition halls, a hotel and the Pinacoteca Agnelli art gallery beneath a glass pavilion.

locations.name: Manifattura Tabacchi
locations.setting: Former state tobacco factory in Florence, redeveloped into a mixed district with courtyards, industrial-style halls and a dedicated events venue called Motel.
locations.facilities: The Motel event space (Building B3, available from March 2026) has 3,000 sqm of usable area, offered in configurations of 500, 1,000 or 1,500 sqm.
locations.suitability: The venue's own page lists fashion shows, photo shoots and conventions among permitted uses, and describes the space as a film and television location.

locations.name: Masseria Marinella
locations.setting: A working fortified farmhouse estate on the plateau outside Altamura, with whitewashed courtyard buildings, olive groves and grazing land typical of the Murgia countryside.

locations.name: MAXXI - National Museum of 21st Century Arts
locations.setting: Zaha Hadid's 2010 museum building in Rome, built on the site of a former army barracks, with curving concrete galleries, a black steel staircase and large open exhibition halls.

locations.name: Mercato Centrale Firenze
locations.setting: Nineteenth-century iron-and-glass covered market near San Lorenzo in Florence, with a ground-floor produce market and an upper-floor food hall of stalls and communal tables.

locations.name: Milano Centrale Railway Station
locations.setting: Monumental 1931 railway terminus in Milan with a vast steel-and-glass train shed, marble ticket halls and Art Deco and Assyrian-influenced decoration across several levels.
locations.suitability: The national rail operator's site states that its stations can host film and TV sets, photo shoots, commercials and music videos, subject to advance email notice to reorganise station flows. Note: the page covers the station network generally (it names Napoli Centrale and Torino Porta Susa as examples) and does not name Milano Centrale specifically.
locations.logistics: Filming requests go through productplacement@fsitaliane.it (own site).

locations.name: Mole Antonelliana - National Cinema Museum
locations.setting: Nineteenth-century domed landmark in Turin housing the National Cinema Museum, with a spiral ramp, a central exhibition hall beneath the dome and a glass panoramic lift to the top.
locations.suitability: The museum's own event page states its spaces lend themselves to photo shoots and film/TV productions, with a separate contact for filming and photography requests (comunicazione@museocinema.it) distinct from press enquiries (ufficiostampa@museocinema.it).

locations.name: MUSE - Science Museum of Trento
locations.setting: Renzo Piano's 2013 science museum in Trento, a stepped glass and steel structure across several floors of exhibition space, part of the redeveloped Le Albere riverside district.

locations.name: Museo del Vetro di Piegaro
locations.setting: A former nineteenth-century glass furnace in the hill town of Piegaro, converted into a museum that preserves the kilns and displays glassware made on site until the factory closed in 1968.

locations.name: OGR Torino
locations.setting: Former 19th-century railway repair workshop in Turin, restored into a steel-and-glass exhibition and event hall with an attached production and rehearsal wing.
locations.facilities: The corporate events page lists two main halls: one of 4,000 sqm (including stage and backstage) holding up to 2,750 people standing in an empty configuration, and a second hall of 300 sqm with a maximum of 150 seated theatre-style, rented empty with no in-house technical equipment. A staffed cloakroom holds up to 900 items.
locations.logistics: Loading access for large vehicles is about 30 m from the stage for the main hall and about 20 m from the second hall, with level access throughout (own site).

locations.name: Ortigia
locations.setting: Historic island core of Syracuse in Sicily, with a baroque cathedral built into the columns of a Greek temple, narrow lanes, a waterfront promenade and a Norman castle at its tip.

locations.name: PalaFlorio
locations.setting: An indoor arena in Bari used for basketball, concerts and trade events, with tiered seating around a large flat floor.

locations.name: Palazzo dei Congressi, EUR
locations.setting: Rationalist congress hall in Rome's EUR district, built for a cancelled 1942 world's fair, with a marble facade, a colonnaded portico and a large domed hall, managed by EUR SpA.
locations.facilities: The venue's own page states: 30,000 sqm total surface, Salone della Cultura 1,450 sqm with 27 m ceiling height, Auditorium Capitalis 792 seats, Terrazza posteriore amphitheatre for 500, Foyer Kennedy and Foyer Arte 800 sqm each, Terrazza frontale 1,085 sqm, a rear stage area of 774 sqm, and up to 26 meeting rooms ranging from 20 to 250 person capacity.
locations.logistics: The site states 1,600 hotel rooms lie within a 2.5 km radius.

locations.name: Piscina delle Rose
locations.setting: A 1950s open-air lido in Rome's EUR district, with a large rectangular pool, sunbathing terraces and Rationalist-style changing pavilions.

locations.name: Porticoes of Bologna
locations.setting: Covered walkways lining central Bologna's streets, including the roughly 3.8 km arcade climbing to the Sanctuary of San Luca, a UNESCO World Heritage arrangement of porticoes.

locations.name: Porto Antico di Genova
locations.setting: Nineteenth-century harbour warehouses and docks in Genoa, redeveloped for Expo 1992 into a waterfront of piazzas, a marina, an aquarium and event spaces along the old quays.
locations.facilities: The site lists 13 halls of varying capacity across the complex, 8,500 sqm gross of exhibition space in the Magazzini del Cotone modules, and a total complex area of 130,000 sqm, stating it hosts over 250 events a year.
locations.suitability: The venue's own page describes the complex as a setting for photo and video shoots.

locations.name: Porto di Gioia Tauro
locations.setting: Italy's largest container transshipment port on the Calabrian coast, with long quays, gantry cranes and stacked container yards handling international freight.

photo.author: The original uploader was Istvánka at Hungarian Wikipedia.

locations.name: Porto Vecchio di Trieste
locations.setting: Disused free port in Trieste with about seventy hectares of 19th-century warehouses, rail sidings and quays between the city centre and the sea, now under partial redevelopment.

locations.name: Real Fabbrica di San Leucio
locations.setting: A royal silk-manufacturing complex built by the Bourbon court above Caserta, with weaving halls, workers' housing and machinery from its eighteenth-century silk mill, part of the Caserta Palace UNESCO site.

locations.name: San Siro Stadium (Stadio Giuseppe Meazza)
locations.setting: Multi-tiered football stadium in Milan shared by AC Milan and Inter, with a distinctive spiral-ramp exterior and seating for over 75,000.
locations.facilities: The stadium's event page states it has 40 hospitality rooms totalling 3,160 sqm, with a combined event capacity of 2,154 people (1,264 for seated dinners), across Sala Executive 1-3, Sala Arancio, Sky Lounge, Sky Box and Sala Interviste. This is hospitality/event capacity, not match-day stadium capacity.

locations.name: Sassi di Matera
locations.setting: Ancient cave-dwelling districts carved into a limestone ravine, frequently standing in for biblical-era Jerusalem.
locations.known_for: The Passion of the Christ (2004), Wonder Woman (2017), No Time to Die (2021)

locations.name: Stadio Olimpico
locations.setting: Rome's main stadium in the Foro Italico complex, with tiered seating for over 70,000 used for football, athletics, concerts and other large events.

locations.name: Teatro alla Scala
locations.setting: 1778 opera house in central Milan with a gilded horseshoe auditorium, tiered boxes, a museum wing and a stage house used for opera, ballet and concerts.

locations.name: Teatro Massimo
locations.setting: Largest opera house in Italy, in central Palermo, with a neoclassical facade, a horseshoe auditorium seating around 1,300 and backstage and rehearsal spaces.

locations.name: Teatro Petruzzelli
locations.setting: Bari's late nineteenth-century opera house, one of Italy's largest theatres, rebuilt after a 1991 fire with its horseshoe auditorium and gilded boxes restored.

locations.name: Toledo Metro Station
locations.setting: Underground metro station in central Naples built around 40 metres deep, with a mosaic-lined vaulted concourse known as the Crater de Luz, part of the city's art-station network.

locations.name: Tropea
locations.setting: Clifftop town on Calabria's Tyrrhenian coast, with a historic centre of stone lanes and balconies overlooking the beach and the offshore Santa Maria dell'Isola sanctuary.

locations.name: Villa del Balbianello
locations.setting: Eighteenth-century villa on a wooded promontory of Lake Como with terraced gardens and open lake panoramas, now a FAI heritage property.
locations.known_for: Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (2002), Casino Royale (2006)
locations.facilities: The venue's own page gives room-by-room figures: La Loggia Durini 60 sqm (ceremony 80-100 people, max 60 seated), Terrazzo a Lago 240 sqm (dinners up to 130), Loggia 90 sqm indoor (dinners up to 75) or 170 sqm indoor plus outdoor (up to 100), Terrazzo Canfora 80 sqm (standing buffet up to 100).
locations.suitability: The site states the villa hosts ceremonies, receptions, corporate meetings and 'set cinematografici e pubblicitari' (film and advertising shoots), and says it has served as the backdrop for numerous film and advertising productions. Photo services such as weddings are paid and require advance booking via a named contact.

locations.name: Villa Necchi Campiglio
locations.setting: 1930s rationalist villa in central Milan designed by Piero Portaluppi, with period interiors, a garden, swimming pool and tennis court, run as a house museum by FAI.
locations.facilities: The venue's own page lists: Sale Pomara Scibetta (basement), 3 adjoining multipurpose rooms totalling 200 sqm; Sala da Pranzo, 43 sqm on the piano nobile; a multipurpose hall of 380 sqm plus a service block (4 toilets, cloakroom, technical room) in the former tennis-court building, with heating and air conditioning; and a garden of 2,000 sqm, partly walkable, with a historic non-swimmable pool.
locations.suitability: The site states the villa is used for photo and film shoots ('set fotografici e cinematografici') and names 'Io sono l'amore' (I Am Love, Luca Guadagnino) and 'House of Gucci' (Ridley Scott) as productions filmed there.

locations.name: Blue Lagoon, Comino
locations.setting: Shallow turquoise channel between Comino and the islet of Cominotto, with white sand under clear water and low limestone cliffs on both shores.

locations.name: Domvs Romana
locations.setting: A Roman-era townhouse excavated at Rabat next to Mdina, with in-situ mosaic floors under a purpose-built museum pavilion managed by Heritage Malta.

locations.name: Dwejra
locations.setting: Rocky bay on Gozo's west coast with an inland sea joined to the open water by a natural tunnel, on a stretch of coastline once marked by the collapsed Azure Window.
locations.known_for: Game of Thrones (season 1), Clash of the Titans (2010)

locations.name: Fort Manoel
locations.setting: Baroque star fort built 1723 to 1755 on its own islet in Marsamxett Harbour, restored with bastions, a chapel and a large open parade ground used for big set builds.
locations.known_for: Assassin's Creed (2016), World War Z (2013), By the Sea (2015)

locations.name: Fort Ricasoli
locations.setting: Vast 17th-century bastioned fort at the mouth of the Grand Harbour whose open parade grounds host large-scale open-air set builds.

locations.name: Fort St Elmo
locations.setting: Star-shaped sixteenth-century fort at the tip of the Valletta peninsula, now home to the National War Museum, with bastions, a parade ground and sea-facing ramparts.
locations.suitability: Listed under Heritage Malta's Exclusive Venues programme as available for product launches, fashion shows, location shoots, corporate meetings, conferences, fine dining events, seminars, weddings and exhibitions. No price or capacity is published; enquiries go through the Exclusive Venues contact form.

locations.name: Is-Suq tal-Belt
locations.setting: Valletta's restored Victorian-era iron market hall on Merchant Street, now a food court and market with its original cast-iron structure kept intact.

locations.name: Malta Aviation Museum
locations.setting: An aircraft collection on the former RAF Ta' Qali airfield, with hangars, several WWII-era aircraft under restoration and open apron space.

locations.name: Malta Film Studios
locations.setting: State-run studio facility whose two vast exterior water tanks sit on the shoreline so their surfaces blend into the natural sea horizon, complemented by an indoor insert tank.
locations.known_for: Raise the Titanic (1980), U-571 (2000), Captain Phillips (2013)

locations.name: Malta International Airport
locations.setting: Malta's only commercial airport, at Luqa, with a single passenger terminal, aircraft apron and a public viewing area, serving as the island's main air gateway.

locations.name: Malta Maritime Museum
locations.setting: Former Royal Naval bakery on the Vittoriosa waterfront, now a museum of Malta's dockyards and Grand Harbour shipping history from the Knights to the twentieth century.
locations.known_for: Malta Story (1953, depicting the wartime dockyards)
locations.suitability: Listed under Heritage Malta's Exclusive Venues programme as available for product launches, fashion shows, location shoots, corporate meetings, conferences, fine dining events, seminars, weddings and exhibitions. No price or capacity is published; enquiries go through the Exclusive Venues contact form.

locations.name: Manoel Theatre
locations.setting: Baroque theatre opened in 1732 in central Valletta, one of Europe's oldest still in use, with a gilded three-tier horseshoe auditorium seating around 620.

locations.name: Mdina
locations.setting: Walled medieval hilltop city of narrow honey-coloured limestone streets, baroque palaces and a monumental main gate.

locations.name: Palazzo Parisio
locations.setting: Eighteenth-century palace remodelled in the 1860s with gilded salons, frescoed halls and Italianate walled gardens with an orangery and grotto.
locations.suitability: The venue's own site lists filming among the activities it hosts, alongside weddings, product launches and fashion shows.

locations.name: Popeye Village
locations.setting: Wooden waterfront village built as the full-scale set for the 1980 Popeye musical, kept afterwards on Anchor Bay as a walk-through attraction.

locations.name: Spazju Kreattiv (St James Cavalier)
locations.setting: A 16th-century artillery cavalier beside Valletta's city gate, converted into a cultural centre with a cinema, a theatre space and gallery rooms.

locations.name: The Inquisitor's Palace
locations.setting: The former seat and prison of the Roman Inquisition in Birgu, a medieval and baroque building with courtrooms, cells and a walled courtyard, managed by Heritage Malta.

locations.name: The Xara Palace
locations.setting: A 17th-century palazzo built into Mdina's bastion walls, converted into a small hotel with period rooms, a rooftop restaurant and views over the surrounding countryside.

locations.name: University of Malta
locations.setting: Main university campus at Tal-Qroqq, with lecture halls, a library and a mix of 1960s and later buildings spread over a hillside site near Msida.

locations.name: Valletta Cruise Port
locations.setting: The cruise and ferry terminal on Valletta's Grand Harbour waterfront, with quaysides below the bastions, former warehouses converted into shops, and views across to the Three Cities.

locations.name: Valletta Design Cluster
locations.setting: Restored eighteenth-century Ospizio building in Valletta, later a hospital and armoury, now converted into shared workspaces and studios for Malta's creative economy.

locations.name: Valletta Historic Centre
locations.setting: UNESCO-listed sixteenth-century fortified capital on a narrow peninsula, its grid of limestone streets lined with baroque churches, auberges and balconied townhouses.
locations.known_for: World War Z (2013), Murder on the Orient Express (2017), By the Sea (2015)

locations.name: Valletta Waterfront
locations.setting: Row of restored eighteenth-century baroque warehouses along the Grand Harbour quayside, now a strip of restaurants, bars and shops beside the cruise terminal.
locations.facilities: Magazino Hall (built 1727) holds up to 400 guests standing, and has an arched limestone ceiling, an adjoining 130 sq m outdoor courtyard, air conditioning, wifi, on-site parking and drive-in access for staging. The Promenade is a 275 m waterfront walkway lined with food and beverage outlets. Sagrestia Vault & the Chapel is a 16th-century vault with an attached chapel, a separate back-of-house entrance, air conditioning and an outdoor patio.
locations.suitability: Under the Stars, an open-air venue on the promenade, is described on the site as having been filmed and photographed by many productions. No filming-specific rules or permit requirements are published for any of the four venue spaces.
locations.logistics: On-site discounted parking, plus coach, minibus and private car parking, is available; Magazino Hall and Under the Stars both offer drive-in access for staging and equipment, and Under the Stars has no height restriction for staging.

locations.name: Ahoy Rotterdam
locations.setting: Multi-hall arena and convention complex in Rotterdam-Zuid with a 16,000-capacity main arena, used for sport, concerts and the 2021 Eurovision Song Contest.

locations.name: Airborne Museum Hartenstein
locations.setting: A nineteenth-century villa in Oosterbeek that served as the British 1st Airborne Division headquarters during the 1944 Battle of Arnhem, now a war museum on the same site.

locations.name: Amsterdam Canal Ring
locations.setting: Seventeenth-century ring of tree-lined canals with gabled townhouses, humpback bridges and houseboats.
locations.known_for: The Fault in Our Stars, Ocean's Twelve

locations.name: Aviodrome
locations.setting: Aviation museum and heritage hangars at Lelystad Airport with historic aircraft including a DC-2, DC-3 and Fokker airliners on static and taxiway display.

locations.name: Bataviawerf (Batavialand)
locations.setting: Working historic shipyard in Lelystad building full-size replica VOC ships beside a reconstructed seventeenth-century harbour, sail loft and rigging sheds.
locations.suitability: Small shoots (up to 4 people) allowed during opening hours with 2 working days notice; larger productions get exclusive access outside opening hours with 10 working days notice

locations.name: Blokhuispoort
locations.setting: Former nineteenth-century prison in Leeuwarden with a star-shaped cell wing, converted into a cultural venue with a library, hostel and workspaces.

locations.name: Der Aa-kerk
locations.setting: A deconsecrated medieval church in the city of Groningen, used today as a venue for exhibitions, concerts and hired events.

locations.name: Erasmusbrug
locations.setting: Asymmetric cable-stayed bridge with a 139-metre bent steel pylon spanning the Nieuwe Maas against the Rotterdam skyline.

locations.name: Euroborg
locations.setting: A multifunctional stadium in the city of Groningen, home ground of football club FC Groningen, with business suites and function rooms hired out for events and weddings.

locations.name: Euromast
locations.setting: 185-metre observation tower beside Rotterdam's Park, with a rotating Euroscoop deck near the top giving a panoramic view over the city and harbour.

locations.name: Fort bij Vechten
locations.setting: Nineteenth-century fortress of the New Dutch Waterline near Bunnik, with brick casemates, powder magazines and grass-covered ramparts around a moat.

locations.name: Forum Groningen
locations.setting: Contemporary multi-storey public library and culture building on Groningen's Grote Markt, with a rooftop terrace, cinema and stacked glass atria.

locations.name: Giethoorn
locations.setting: Car-free village of thatched farmhouses linked by canals, footbridges and punting boats in the Overijssel peatlands, part of the Weerribben-Wieden wetland.

locations.name: Grand Hotel Karel V
locations.setting: A hotel in central Utrecht built around a former commandery of the Teutonic Order that later served as a military barracks and hospital, with gardens and rooms for hire.

locations.name: Groninger Museum
locations.setting: A museum in the city of Groningen in a brightly coloured postmodern building designed with Alessandro Mendini, with galleries and event spaces available for hire.

locations.name: Grote Kerk Veere
locations.setting: A large late-gothic former church in the small Zeeland town of Veere, deconsecrated and now used as an exhibition and events space available for hire.

locations.name: Herinneringscentrum Kamp Westerbork
locations.setting: The site of a Second World War transit camp near Hooghalen from which over 100,000 people were deported, now a memorial centre with a visitor centre and archive.

locations.name: Hoge Veluwe National Park
locations.setting: A 5,400-hectare national park of drift sand, heathland and pine forest on the Veluwe, home to the Kroller-Muller Museum and free-roaming red deer and wild boar.

locations.name: Hoog Catharijne
locations.setting: A large indoor shopping centre next to Utrecht Centraal station with shops, restaurants and public concourses that have served as a backdrop for productions.

locations.name: Hotel New York
locations.setting: A hotel and restaurant on Rotterdam's Wilhelminapier in the former head office of the Holland America Line, with period interiors and function rooms for hire.

locations.name: Ir. D.F. Woudagemaal
locations.setting: A steam-powered pumping station near Lemmer, built in 1920 and still operational, among the largest of its kind, with meeting arrangements available on site.

locations.name: Jaarbeurs Utrecht
locations.setting: A large convention, trade fair and event complex next to Utrecht Centraal station, with multiple exhibition halls hired out for congresses, fairs and productions.

locations.name: Johan Cruijff ArenA
locations.setting: 55,000-seat retractable-roof stadium in Amsterdam Zuidoost, home to Ajax, with a bowl of tiered stands usable for matches, concerts and productions.

locations.name: Kinderdijk
locations.setting: UNESCO World Heritage polder landscape south-east of Rotterdam with nineteen eighteenth-century windmills lined along parallel waterways.

locations.name: Kruisherenhotel Maastricht
locations.setting: Fifteenth-century Gothic monastery church and cloister in Maastricht converted into a design hotel, keeping vaulted ceilings, stained glass and a choir loft.
locations.logistics: Hotel closed for renovation; scheduled to reopen October 2026.

locations.name: Kunstlinie
locations.setting: A theatre and exhibition centre in Almere with a business hire programme for its auditoriums and foyers.

locations.name: Kurhaus Den Haag
locations.setting: Grand 1885 beachfront hotel at Scheveningen with a domed Kurzaal ballroom of murals and chandeliers, and terraces facing the North Sea promenade.
locations.facilities: 10 meeting/event halls accommodating up to 1,500 people in total; 270 guest rooms including 8 suites; historic domed Kurzaal hall. Site now operates as Grand Hotel Amrath Kurhaus (amrathkurhaus.com); the kurhaus.nl domain redirects there.

locations.name: Lloyd Hotel
locations.setting: Former 1921 emigrant hotel on Amsterdam's eastern docklands, rebuilt with room categories from one to five stars mixing Art Deco and contemporary interiors.
locations.facilities: 136 bedrooms; on-site cocktail bar, brasserie, meeting spaces and private dining. Site now operates as The Hoxton, Amsterdam (thehoxton.com/amsterdam/lloyd/); the lloydhotel.com domain redirects there.
locations.logistics: 50 on-site parking spaces at EUR 3.50/hour or EUR 35/day.

locations.name: LocHal
locations.setting: A former railway repair workshop in Tilburg's Spoorzone, converted into a public library and culture hall that is marketed as an events and business location.

locations.name: Loonse en Drunense Duinen
locations.setting: Inland drift-sand dune area of around 2,000 hectares between Tilburg and 's-Hertogenbosch, with open sand plains, marram grass and pine forest edges.

locations.name: Louis Hartlooper Complex
locations.setting: Former 1921 courthouse in Utrecht converted into an arthouse cinema and cafe, with a wood-panelled former courtroom now used as a screening room.

locations.name: Maassilo
locations.setting: A former grain silo and elevator on Rotterdam's Maashaven, converted into a club, concert and business events venue while keeping its raw concrete industrial interior.

locations.name: Maeslantkering / Keringhuis
locations.setting: Giant swinging steel storm surge barrier at Hoek van Holland guarding the Nieuwe Waterweg, each of its two arms as long as the Eiffel Tower is high.

locations.name: Manteling van Walcheren
locations.setting: Dune woodland and beach reserve on the Walcheren coast near Domburg and Oostkapelle, combining old estate woods with open dunes and North Sea beach.

locations.name: Markthal Rotterdam
locations.setting: Arched 2014 market hall in Rotterdam with a horseshoe of apartments wrapped around a food market floor of stalls, restaurants and a barrel-vaulted ceiling mural.

locations.name: Media Park Hilversum
locations.setting: Television production campus in Hilversum with large audience studios such as Studio 21 and 22 and most national broadcasters on site.
locations.known_for: The Voice of Holland, The Voice Kids
locations.facilities: Studio 21 is offered as an event location with a 360 m2 LED screen, sound installation and light ceiling; the park houses over 100 media companies including NOS, RTL, NEP, EMG and ITV, with restaurants, a gym, a hair and makeup salon and childcare on site.
locations.suitability: A private business park without public opening hours; employees need a valid access pass and visitors are welcome around event start times. Studio specifications and rental terms are not published on the park's own site.
locations.logistics: Joop van den Endeplein 1, Hilversum: own railway station Hilversum Media Park with four trains an hour and a footbridge into the park; by car via A1 exit 9 Laren/Hilversum; 24-hour parking deck and garage A at EUR 2.00 per hour, card payment only.

locations.name: Museum Buurtspoorweg
locations.setting: Heritage narrow-gauge railway between Haaksbergen and Boekelo near the German border, with early twentieth-century steam trains and a period station building.

locations.name: Museum Steam Tram Hoorn-Medemblik
locations.setting: Heritage steam railway running 20 kilometres between Hoorn and Medemblik, with restored period carriages, a working locomotive shed and historic stations.

locations.name: NDSM Wharf
locations.setting: Former shipyard on the IJ in Amsterdam-Noord with a vast former assembly hall, dry docks and cranes, now used for events and creative work.
locations.suitability: Commercial shoots require permission and a location contract; a free notification to the municipality (gemeente) is mandatory for commercial use. Small-scale personal shoots (up to 3 people, non-commercial) are permitted under conditions. Public artworks on site cannot be occupied for longer than 15 minutes.

locations.name: NEMO Science Museum
locations.setting: Renzo Piano-designed green, ship-shaped science museum rising from the water at Amsterdam's Oosterdok, with a sloped public roof terrace and open exhibition floors.

locations.name: Netherlands Open Air Museum
locations.setting: Open-air heritage museum near Arnhem with more than 80 relocated historic Dutch buildings, farmhouses and windmills arranged as period villages around a working canal.

locations.name: Oosterscheldekering / Neeltje Jans
locations.setting: Nine-kilometre storm surge barrier across the Oosterschelde estuary with 62 movable steel gates on concrete piers, its visitor centre on the artificial island of Neeltje Jans.

locations.name: Oostvaardersplassen
locations.setting: A large wetland nature reserve between Almere and Lelystad, reclaimed from the former Zuiderzee seabed, used as the setting for wildlife documentaries.

locations.name: Paleis Het Loo
locations.setting: A former royal residence on the edge of Apeldoorn, open as a national museum with formal gardens and rooms hired out for exhibitions and events.

locations.name: Pathe Tuschinski
locations.setting: 1921 Art Deco and Amsterdam School cinema on the Reguliersbreestraat, with an ornate auditorium, stained glass, mosaics and a sweeping foyer staircase.

locations.name: Philips Stadion
locations.setting: 35,000-seat home stadium of PSV in Eindhoven, with four continuous tiers of covered seating around the pitch.

locations.name: Radio Kootwijk
locations.setting: Isolated 1920s Expressionist transmitter hall on the Veluwe heathland, a monumental concrete radio station known as Building A, now used for events and productions.

locations.name: Rietveld Schroder House
locations.setting: UNESCO-listed 1924 De Stijl house in Utrecht by Gerrit Rietveld, with sliding partition walls, primary-colour accents and a flexible open first floor.

locations.name: Rijksmuseum Twenthe
locations.setting: An art museum in Enschede with historic and modern collections, hosting exhibitions and business events in its galleries.

locations.name: Rodahal
locations.setting: A multipurpose events and concert hall in Kerkrade marketed for business parties, concerts and sports events.

locations.name: Sint-Pietersberg / ENCI Quarry
locations.setting: Former limestone quarry on the southern edge of Maastricht, now a reclaimed nature area of white marl cliffs, terraces and a lake beside the old cement works.

locations.name: Sonneveld House
locations.setting: Fully furnished 1933 Nieuwe Bouwen villa in Rotterdam with period Functionalist interiors, tubular steel furniture and built-in fittings kept intact.

locations.name: SS Rotterdam
locations.setting: 1959 ocean liner of the Holland America Line permanently moored in Rotterdam, kept with original Art Deco and mid-century interiors, now a hotel and museum ship.
locations.facilities: Multiple event rooms aboard ship: Smoking Room (150 people), Grand Ballroom (450), Glass Enclosed Promenade (250), Atlantic Promenade (500), Odyssee Room (350), La Fontaine Room (350), Upper Promenade Deck (10), Promenade Deck (999).

locations.name: Strijp-S
locations.setting: Former closed Philips factory campus in Eindhoven redeveloped into a creative district of brick industrial halls, courtyards and new residential towers.

locations.name: Theater aan het Vrijthof
locations.setting: A theatre on Maastricht's central Vrijthof square with multiple stages, offering its auditoriums and foyers for business hire alongside its regular programme.

locations.name: Thialf
locations.setting: Indoor 400-metre speed skating arena in Heerenveen with tiered seating for around 12,500 spectators, also used for concerts and events on the ice floor.

locations.name: TT Circuit Assen
locations.setting: A permanent motor racing circuit near Assen in use since 1955, host of the Dutch MotoGP round and hired out for other events outside race weekends.

locations.name: Van Nelle Factory
locations.setting: UNESCO-listed 1931 factory in Rotterdam built for processing coffee, tea and tobacco, with steel-framed glass curtain walls and an elevated conveyor bridge.

locations.name: Veenhuizen Prison Museum
locations.setting: Former nineteenth-century penal colony building in Veenhuizen, part of the UNESCO Colonies of Benevolence, with cell blocks, courtyards and institutional corridors.

locations.name: Veluwsche Stoomtrein Maatschappij
locations.setting: Heritage steam and diesel railway between Apeldoorn and Dieren through Veluwe forest, with a restored 1887 station and period rolling stock at Beekbergen.

locations.name: Verkadefabriek
locations.setting: A former Verkade biscuit factory in 's-Hertogenbosch converted into a culture centre with theatre halls, cinema screens, a cafe and business hire.

locations.name: Watersnoodmuseum
locations.setting: A museum near Ouwerkerk built inside four Phoenix caissons that were used to close the last dike breach after the 1953 flood disaster, with halls available for group and business bookings.

locations.name: Westergasfabriek
locations.setting: Former nineteenth-century coal gasworks in Amsterdam converted into an events site with several brick halls, a cobbled courtyard and a surrounding park.

photo.author: No machine-readable author provided. Arch assumed (based on copyright claims).

locations.name: Wilhelminabrug
locations.setting: Steel arch road bridge over the IJssel at Deventer, used as the stand-in Arnhem bridge for the 1977 film A Bridge Too Far because the real bridge's surroundings had changed too much.

locations.name: Wilminktheater en Muziekcentrum
locations.setting: A theatre and concert hall in Enschede's Nationaal Muziekkwartier with a business and venue-hire programme alongside its performance schedule.

locations.name: WTC Expo Leeuwarden
locations.setting: A convention and exhibition centre in Leeuwarden with several halls hired out for congresses, fairs and business events.

locations.name: Zaanse Schans
locations.setting: A relocated riverside hamlet of wooden houses, workshops and working windmills in Zaanstad, run as a heritage attraction with its own business events programme.

locations.name: Zonnestraal Sanatorium
locations.setting: Modernist 1928 former tuberculosis sanatorium near Hilversum by architect Jan Duiker, with steel-framed pavilions, large glass walls and a wooded park setting.

locations.name: Zuid-Limburgse Stoomtrein Maatschappij
locations.setting: Heritage steam railway through the South Limburg hills between Simpelveld, Kerkrade and Vetschau, with vintage carriages and period station buildings.

locations.name: Zuiderzeemuseum
locations.setting: An open-air and indoor museum in Enkhuizen that reconstructs a historic Zuiderzee fishing village with relocated houses, workshops and a working harbour.
locations.facilities: Group and business bookings, meeting rooms, catering

locations.name: Akershus Fortress
locations.setting: Medieval castle on Oslo's harbour promontory, expanded into an 18th-century bastioned fortress, with a stone keep, cobbled courtyards and government reception rooms still in ceremonial use.

locations.name: Atlantic Ocean Road
locations.setting: Eight-kilometre stretch of County Road 64 hopping between skerries on a chain of bridges, including the curved Storseisundet Bridge, exposed to open sea on both sides.

locations.name: Bastøy Prison
locations.setting: Low-security island prison in the Oslofjord run on an open, self-sufficient farming regime, with wooden former manor buildings alongside newer institutional blocks.
locations.known_for: King of Devil's Island (2010), Where to Invade Next (2015), Sicko (2007, DVD extras)

locations.name: Dagslys Studios
locations.setting: Five purpose-built stages from 81 to 500 square metres in Nydalen, Oslo, with lighting and grip rental, workshops, props storage and costume and makeup rooms in the same building.
locations.facilities: Five studios of 500, 211, 137, 124 and 81 m2 with shared makeup and costume fitting areas, showers, a dining space for 30, art department and props storage, a carpentry workshop and production offices; lighting, camera, generator and truck rental in the same building.
locations.suitability: Studios and equipment are rented for any media and film production, with 24-hour equipment delivery; part of Oslo Film Studios.
locations.logistics: Gjerdrums vei 6, Nydalen, Oslo

locations.name: FilmCamp
locations.setting: A production hub in a former military base at Overbygd in Malselv, with sound stages, offices, accommodation and catering used as a base for shoots across the Arctic landscape of Troms.
locations.facilities: Three main studios plus one smaller studio with wooden floors, two soundproofed studios, offices, meeting rooms, accommodation, catering and a pub
locations.logistics: Located at Tomas Tomassens vei 41, 9334 Overbygd, reachable by plane and bus

locations.name: Filmparken
locations.setting: A film and TV production site in Jar outside Oslo that has hosted continuous film production since 1935, with three sound stages, a smaller studio and a costume rental department.
locations.facilities: Three main studios plus one smaller studio with wooden floors, two soundproofed studios, costume rental with wardrobe staff
locations.logistics: Located at Wedel Jarlsbergs vei 36, 1358 Jar, about 15 minutes from central Oslo

locations.name: Håkonshallen
locations.setting: Stone royal reception hall built in the 1250s inside Bergenhus fortress, rebuilt after a 1944 harbour explosion, with a vaulted timber-roofed great hall used for concerts and ceremonies.

photo.author: User:Sveter (Please credit as "Petr Šmerkl, Wikipedia" in case you use this outside WMF projects.)

locations.name: Hamar Cathedral Ruins (Domkirkeodden)
locations.setting: Ruins of a medieval stone cathedral on a headland by Lake Mjøsa, enclosed since 1998 in a modern glass and steel protective dome, part of a wider open-air history museum site.

locations.name: Hardangerbadet
locations.setting: An indoor swimming pool in Oystese with floor to ceiling windows over the Hardangerfjord, listed as a filming location by the Norwegian Film Commission.

locations.name: Hartvig Nissen School
locations.setting: Working upper secondary school building from 1899 in Oslo's Frogner district, a brick institutional building with classrooms and a courtyard used as the real setting for a teen drama series.

locations.name: Lyse Abbey
locations.setting: The moss covered ruins of a medieval monastery near Bergen, with stone arches and columns around a grass courtyard, listed as a historic filming location by the Western Norway Film Commission.
locations.known_for: Mission: Impossible - Fallout, Black Widow, Succession (productions cited for Western Norway generally)

locations.name: Njardarheimr Viking Valley
locations.setting: Reconstructed Viking-age settlement of turf-roofed timber longhouses and workshops at the head of Nærøyfjorden, built and staffed as a living-history village.

locations.name: Odda Public Swimming Pool
locations.setting: Indoor municipal swimming pool in the former industrial town of Odda at the head of the Sørfjord, run as a public bathhouse with scheduled sessions for the local community.

locations.name: Preikestolen (Pulpit Rock)
locations.setting: Flat granite cliff ledge about 600 metres above Lysefjord, reached only by a four-kilometre mountain hiking trail.

locations.name: Sagene Folkebad
locations.setting: Indoor public bathhouse from 1899 in late-historicist style beside the Akerselva river, with arched windows and a period stair hall, still operating as a pool and rehabilitation facility.

locations.name: Sentralen
locations.setting: A former bank building in central Oslo converted into a cultural and event house with about 30 rentable rooms, including a grand hall that was once the bank's customer hall.
locations.facilities: About 30 venues from small meeting rooms to Marmorsalen for up to 1,000 people, former bank vaults, event recording and streaming services
locations.logistics: Located at Ovre Slottsgate 3, central Oslo, close to public transport

locations.name: Stavanger Swimming Hall
locations.setting: Municipal indoor pool completed in 1971 next to Stavanger city hall, built in exposed concrete with a 25-metre pool, diving tower and separate children's pool.

locations.name: Vemork
locations.setting: Former hydroelectric and heavy-water plant on a gorge above Rjukan, with a monumental early-20th-century industrial facade, now a museum reached by cable car or an 8 km sabotage trail.
locations.known_for: Kampen om tungtvannet (1948), The Heroes of Telemark (1965), Kampen om tungtvannet / The Saboteurs (TV series, 2015)

locations.name: Vestkantbadet Sommerro
locations.setting: An Art Deco indoor swimming pool with mosaic murals inside the redeveloped Sommerro complex in central Oslo, listed as an interior filming location by the Norwegian Film Commission.

locations.name: Vinje Church
locations.setting: Wooden cross-shaped parish church built in 1796 in the rural Vinje valley, seating around 225, with a painted interior altarpiece and carved benches from the 1930s.

locations.name: Alvernia Studios
locations.setting: A domed studio complex near Krakow with multiple sound stages and a large blue-screen hall, built on a former limestone quarry site 18 kilometres from Krakow Airport.
locations.facilities: Facilities include a recording studio, photography studios (K-03, K-04, K-05), colour correction suites including a 4K colour correction room, a motion capture and rehearsal space, sound and image post-production suites, and production offices.

locations.name: Areszt Śledczy w Zabrzu (Zabrze Remand Prison)
locations.setting: A closed remand prison in Zabrze built in 1888 in the style of German 19th-century prison architecture, with around 290 cells across four wings, shut down in 2018.

locations.name: ATM Studio
locations.setting: Film and television production centre of around 14,000 square metres in Warsaw's Wawer district, with multiple soundstages, TV studios, production offices and post-production facilities.
locations.known_for: The Voice of Poland, Dancing with the Stars: Taniec z gwiazdami
locations.facilities: Six halls totalling 5,200 m2: Hall A 1,500 m2 (45 x 34 m, 12 m high), Halls B to E 800 m2 each (32 x 25 m, 6 to 7 m high) and Hall F 500 m2; 14 dressing rooms of 34 m2 and two VIP dressing rooms of 60 m2, eight makeup rooms, scenic warehouses of 110 to 440 m2, a 3,900 kg cargo lift, catering and conference rooms on a 14,000 m2 site.
locations.suitability: Offers set design and construction, lighting and sound, post-production and VFX, costume and prop rental, OB vans and a virtual studio; two 4 MVA transformer stations, per-hall power connections from 16 A to 400 A, fibre links for nationwide TV transmission and silent ventilation for sound recording. Quotes on request.
locations.logistics: Wal Miedzeszynski 384, Wawer district, about 12 km from Warsaw city centre; three independent parking areas.

locations.name: Catholic University of Lublin (KUL)
locations.setting: A university in Lublin founded in 1918, with a historic main building on Aleje Raclawickie housing faculties, libraries and archives that include manuscripts by Adam Mickiewicz.

locations.name: Cavatina Hall
locations.setting: A large glass-fronted concert and conference hall in Bielsko-Biala, opened in 2023, shortlisted as a finalist in the regional Silesian Film Location 2024 competition.

locations.name: Centennial Hall
locations.setting: A UNESCO-listed 1913 reinforced-concrete domed hall in Wroclaw, seating up to 6,000 beneath a 42-metre ribbed concrete dome, set in surrounding park and garden grounds.

locations.name: Central Museum of Textiles (Biala Fabryka)
locations.setting: A 19th-century cotton mill on Piotrkowska street in Lodz, the White Factory built by Ludwik Geyer, now a textile museum with large weaving halls, a chimney and a steam engine room, with space to hire.
locations.facilities: Wynajem przestrzeni (venue rental) available for events

locations.name: Dworzec PKP Sosnowiec Główny (Sosnowiec Główny Railway Station)
locations.setting: A working railway station in Sosnowiec opened in 1859 on the Warsaw to Katowice line, with a 24-hour main hall, ticket counters and waiting benches.

locations.name: EC1 Lodz
locations.setting: A former coal-fired power station of 1907 in central Lodz, restored as a science and culture centre with its original turbine hall, boiler house and control rooms intact.

locations.name: Elektrownia Powisle
locations.setting: A former Warsaw power station on the Vistula riverside, its turn of the century turbine and boiler halls converted into a retail, dining and event complex while keeping the original brick and steelwork.
locations.facilities: Industrial-style halls for events and exhibitions, food hall, day spa
locations.logistics: ul. Dobra 42, Warsaw, Powisle district

locations.name: Former Halemba-Wirek Mine Demolition Yard
locations.setting: A post-mining industrial complex at the former Halemba-Wirek colliery in Ruda Slaska, with abandoned halls, cranes, storage buildings and a derelict-styled house used for industrial and post-apocalyptic scenes.
locations.facilities: Power and water, parking, briefing room, office space
locations.suitability: Industrial, war, thriller, horror and post-apocalyptic productions, commercials and music videos

locations.name: Former Halemba-Wirek Mine Dismantling Centre
locations.setting: A former coal mine site in Ruda Śląska with intact workshop halls, overhead cranes, technological tracks, warehouses and an abandoned residential building, used mainly for exteriors.
locations.suitability: crime, action, war, historical, thriller, horror and post-apocalyptic productions, automotive commercials, music videos
locations.logistics: on-site office space, briefing room and shower facilities

locations.name: Former synagogue, Zarki (MGOK)
locations.setting: A 19th-century former synagogue in the small town of Zarki, now the municipal cultural centre (MGOK), with power, water and vehicle access offered for filming.

locations.name: Gdansk Shipyard (European Solidarity Centre)
locations.setting: The historic Lenin Shipyard gate and slipways where the Solidarity movement began in 1980, bordered by the European Solidarity Centre's rusted-steel museum building and surviving shipyard halls.
locations.facilities: Auditorium: 483 sq m, up to 417 people, with a 7x11 m stage, a 12x7 m movie screen, 4 simultaneous interpretation booths (8 language channels) and 2 dressing rooms, plus an adjoining 125 sq m mezzanine. Other spaces: Winter Garden 400 sq m, Foyer 500 sq m, Observation Deck 600 sq m (over 25 m high, up to 50 people, seasonal access), Multifunctional Hall 220 sq m (up to 200 people), Library 180 sq m (up to 100 people), Media Library 85 sq m (up to 70 people), Archive Reading Room 72 sq m (up to 30 people), and workshop rooms of 92 sq m (up to 70 people) and 52 sq m (up to 50 people).

locations.name: Hala Koszyki
locations.setting: A 1908 steel-framed market hall in Warsaw's Ochota district, restored behind its original facade into a food hall of restaurants, bars and shops around a glazed central nave.

locations.name: Hel Peninsula
locations.setting: A 35-kilometre sand spit enclosing the Bay of Gdansk, with pine-backed Baltic beaches on its open-sea side and a historic fishing town and former naval base at its tip.

locations.name: Historic Guido Coal Mine
locations.setting: A former working coal mine in Zabrze, now a branch of the Museum of Coal Mining, with underground tours down to 320 metres and a preserved pithead machine hall.

locations.name: Huta Batory director's building
locations.setting: A 1915 modernist administration building at the Huta Batory steelworks in Chorzow, still in office use, with a roof turret, three bas-reliefs over the entrance and an interior courtyard.
locations.facilities: Power and water, parking, meeting rooms, original period interiors

locations.name: ICE Krakow Congress Centre
locations.setting: A congress centre on the Vistula riverbank in Krakow run by the city's development agency, with an auditorium hall, a theatre hall and a chamber hall used for conferences, concerts and theatrical productions.
locations.logistics: ul. Marii Konopnickiej 17, Krakow

locations.name: Juliusz Slowacki Theatre
locations.setting: A late 19th-century municipal theatre on plac Swietego Ducha in Krakow, with an ornate main auditorium plus the smaller Dom Machin and MOS stages, offering building tours and venue hire.

locations.name: Kasprowy Wierch Cable Car
locations.setting: A 1936 aerial cableway climbing from Kuznice to the 1,987-metre summit of Kasprowy Wierch in the Tatras, run in two stages with a mid-station at Myslenickie Turnie.

locations.name: Kazimierz, Kraków
locations.setting: Kraków's former Jewish quarter, where synagogues, cobbled lanes and tenement courtyards still follow the pre-war street layout.

locations.name: Koneser (former Warsaw Vodka Factory)
locations.setting: A former vodka distillery in the Praga district of Warsaw, its 19th-century factory buildings and central plaza now hosting restaurants, shops, galleries and a vodka museum, hired for markets, concerts and exhibitions.
locations.logistics: Plac Konesera 1, Warsaw, Praga-Polnoc district

locations.name: Kopalnia Cwiczebna training mine
locations.setting: An underground mining school in Dabrowa Gornicza with three levels of tunnels, original mechanical and electrical training equipment and brick-lined corridors, part of the Sztygarka municipal museum since 2010.
locations.facilities: Vehicle access, parking, power supply, low light and low noise underground

locations.name: Kościół Św. Wawrzyńca w Mikołowie (Church of St Lawrence, Mikołów)
locations.setting: A brick parish church in the Mokre district of Mikołów, built in the mid-16th century and rebuilt several times, with stained glass windows in its interior.

locations.name: KWK Centrum Coal Mine
locations.setting: A Bytom coal mine, working from 1881 and in liquidation since 2015, with a mining shaft, an escape-apparatus store and a security building still standing among the halls being demolished.
locations.facilities: Vehicle access, on-site production base, parking

locations.name: Lodz Film School (PWSFTviT)
locations.setting: The national film, television and theatre school in Lodz, with shooting halls, screening rooms and post-production labs used by students, and a production history running through Polish cinema since the 1940s.
locations.known_for: Alumni include Andrzej Wajda, Roman Polanski, Krzysztof Kieslowski

locations.name: Manufaktura
locations.setting: Izrael Poznanski's 19th-century red-brick textile mill complex in Lodz, converted into a shopping, leisure and museum quarter around its original factory yard and chimney.

locations.name: MOCAK Museum of Contemporary Art
locations.setting: A contemporary art museum in Krakow's Zablocie district, built into the former administrative building of the Oskar Schindler Enamel Factory, with galleries laid out through the historic industrial structure.
locations.logistics: ul. Lipowa 4, Krakow

locations.name: Muzeum Emigracji (Emigration Museum)
locations.setting: A restored 1930s ocean liner terminal on the Gdynia waterfront, now the Emigration Museum, with its original passenger halls open to visitors and offered as rentable event space.

locations.name: Muzeum Hutnictwa Cynku Walcownia (Zinc Metallurgy Museum)
locations.setting: A zinc-processing museum in the Szopienice district of Katowice covering over 5,000 square metres of former rolling-mill halls, with an intact production line of furnaces and rollers.

locations.name: Muzeum Kinematografii w Łodzi (Museum of Cinematography)
locations.setting: A house museum since 1986 in the former Scheibler family palace on Plac Zwycięstwa in Łódź, whose historic interiors have served as scenography for dozens of Polish films and TV series.

locations.name: National Forum of Music (NFM)
locations.setting: A 2015 concert hall complex on plac Wolnosci in Wroclaw, run jointly by the city, the region and the ministry of culture, with a main hall plus red, black and chamber halls available to hire.

locations.name: Nikiszowiec
locations.setting: A brick workers' housing estate built 1908-1918 for the Giesche coal mine, its enclosed courtyard blocks, arcaded passages and communal bakery still inhabited today.

locations.name: Norblin Factory
locations.setting: A 19th-century metalware factory in the Wola district of Warsaw, its brick production halls preserved as an open-air industrial museum alongside offices, shops and restaurants across a 2 hectare site.
locations.facilities: Atmospheric post-industrial halls used for conferences, premieres, concerts and fashion shows
locations.logistics: ul. Zelazna 51/53, Warsaw, Wola district

locations.name: Nowa Huta
locations.setting: A planned socialist-realist steelworkers' town built from 1949 beside the former Lenin steelworks, with a monumental central square, arcaded avenues and uniform apartment blocks.

locations.name: Ogrodzieniec Castle
locations.setting: Ruined 14th-century castle on the highest hill of the Kraków-Częstochowa Upland, its broken towers rising among limestone outcrops on the Trail of the Eagles' Nests.

locations.name: Opera Lesna (Sopot Forest Opera)
locations.setting: An open-air amphitheatre cut into wooded dunes above Sopot, seating around 4,300 beneath a part-covered stage, home to the annual Sopot Festival.

locations.name: ORP Blyskawica
locations.setting: A Grom-class destroyer launched in 1936 and preserved as a museum ship on Gdynia's waterfront, with its bridge, gun turrets and below-deck compartments open to visitors.
locations.facilities: The museum building (not the ship itself) rents an audiovisual hall for up to 121 people, with daylight and ceiling lighting, a screen and projector, lectern, WiFi, cloakroom and ground-floor toilets, plus a small classroom for up to 15 people. Space in front of the building is not available for hire.

locations.name: Osiedle A
locations.setting: The first planned housing estate of postwar Tychy, built from the 1950s with low modernist blocks around courtyards and green space, named winner of the Silesian Film Location 2024 award.

locations.name: Pałac Kultury Zagłębia (Palace of Culture of Zagłębie)
locations.setting: A 1950s culture centre in Dąbrowa Górnicza designed by Zbigniew Rzepecki, with a cinema hall, theatre stage, wedding hall and gallery still in public use.

locations.name: Palace of Culture and Science
locations.setting: A 237-metre socialist-classicist tower built in 1955 as a gift from the Soviet Union, holding theatres, cinemas, a congress hall, museums and an observation deck over central Warsaw.
locations.facilities: 237 m tall building with 46 floors and 3,288 rooms; the viewing terrace is at 114 m.

locations.name: PGE Narodowy
locations.setting: Warsaw's national stadium of 2011, built on the site of the former Tenth-Anniversary Stadium, with a retractable roof and a facade patterned on the Polish flag.

locations.name: Poznan International Fair (MTP)
locations.setting: Poland's largest trade fair complex in central Poznan, dating from 1921, with 15 pavilions, a congress centre, banqueting spaces and an event plaza used for exhibitions and large-scale events.
locations.facilities: 15 exhibition pavilions, congress centre, underground parking, on-site hotels and restaurants

locations.name: Poznan Town Hall
locations.setting: A Renaissance town hall of 1560 on Poznan's Old Market Square, rebuilt to Italian designs, with an arcaded facade, a mechanical clock with butting goats and a council chamber now a history museum.
