locations.name: Sąd Rejonowy w Sosnowcu (Sosnowiec District Court)
locations.setting: A district court operating since 1945 inside one of the Schön family's eclectic 1903 palaces in Sosnowiec, with courtrooms set in the original ballroom, dining room and library.

locations.name: Spodek
locations.setting: A saucer-shaped 1971 sports and concert arena in central Katowice, its suspended roof spanning a hall seating up to about 11,500 for events.
locations.suitability: A standard filming day covers 12 hours of shooting plus 2 hours for equipment setup and teardown, and includes an electrical connection, a dedicated event manager, a break room and parking; an extra setup/teardown day costs 50 percent of the daily filming rate. Interior photo sessions are allowed subject to the event schedule, roof photography is not permitted, and drone shots must comply with Polish aviation regulations.

locations.name: Stadion Slaski
locations.setting: A bowl stadium built in 1956 on a reclaimed slag heap in Chorzow, rebuilt with a membrane roof and seating around 54,000 for football, speedway and concerts.
locations.facilities: Maximum stand capacity 54,378 (about 30,000 for concerts on the pitch), 2,092 business seats, 384 VIP box seats (22 boxes for 16 people, 1 box for 32), and 106 spaces for visitors with disabilities. Outdoor: an artificial-turf athletics pitch 105x68 m with floodlighting at 500 lx, a natural-turf pitch 94x64 m at 250 lx, 3 tennis courts, a western perimeter area of about 23,000 sq m (asphalt, concrete, grass) and a technical backup area of about 5,000 sq m. Indoor: a conference centre of 1,785 sq m (divisible into 3), a 700 sq m conference hall with 2 retractable stands of 180 seats each, 2 multifunctional halls of 310 sq m each, a 940 sq m main hall, 2 reception/foyer areas of 364 sq m each, a large VIP box of 80 sq m and small VIP boxes of 34 sq m each.

locations.name: Stary Browar
locations.setting: A former brewery in central Poznan converted into a mixed retail, dining and contemporary art complex, with the original brick brewery buildings kept alongside new gallery and shopping spaces.
locations.logistics: ul. Polwiejska 42, Poznan

locations.name: Stary Szpital w Żywcu (Old Hospital, Żywiec)
locations.setting: A disused hospital building on Sienkiewicza street in Żywiec, listed by the regional film commission as a filming site with on-site parking and mains utilities.

locations.name: Superjednostka
locations.setting: A 15-storey slab apartment block in central Katowice built 1967 to 1972 from prefabricated concrete panels raised on stilts, holding 762 flats for about 3,000 residents.

locations.name: Szczecin Philharmonic
locations.setting: An angular glass and white concrete concert hall in Szczecin, winner of the EU Mies van der Rohe architecture award, with a large symphonic hall plus smaller chamber and multimedia halls and a hall rental service.

locations.name: Szkoła Podstawowa w Bieruniu (Bieruń Primary School)
locations.setting: A municipal primary school in Bieruń with an original wing from 1848 extended in later decades, now spread across two buildings with 42 classes and a gym hall.

locations.name: Sztygarka Training Mine (Kopalnia Ćwiczebna)
locations.setting: An underground training mine built in 1927 for mining school students, with three levels of tunnels and period equipment, now a branch of the Sztygarka municipal museum.

locations.name: Teatr Muzyczny im. Danuty Baduszkowej
locations.setting: A musical theatre building on plac Grunwaldzki in Gdynia with the largest musical stage in Poland alongside a new stage and a chamber stage, staging large scale musical productions.

locations.name: Twierdza Boyen (Boyen Fortress)
locations.setting: A 19th-century Prussian fortress in Gizycko with ramparts, a parade ground, a powder laboratory and an armourer's workshop, hosting reenactments, festivals and light shows on its central majdan.
locations.logistics: ul. Turystyczna 1, Gizycko

locations.name: Tyskie Brewery (Tyskie Browary Książęce)
locations.setting: A working brewery in Tychy dating to 1629, with a visitor centre inside its historic industrial buildings, noted by the regional film commission for its industrial character.

locations.name: University of Warsaw Library (BUW)
locations.setting: The main library of the University of Warsaw on the Vistula riverside, combining large glazed reading rooms with a landscaped roof garden above the building, and space available to hire for events.
locations.logistics: ul. Dobra 56/66, Warsaw, Powisle district

locations.name: Vienna House Easy Katowice
locations.setting: A hotel on Sokolska street in central Katowice with a fully glazed ground floor holding the reception, lobby, restaurant and breakfast room in daylight-filled open space.

locations.name: Walcownia Cynku zinc rolling mill
locations.setting: A preserved zinc rolling mill in the Szopienice district of Katowice, built 1903 to 1917, spanning 5,000 square metres with furnaces, casting carousels, rolling mills and four original steam engines.
locations.facilities: Heating and air conditioning, parking, WiFi, power 230/460V 16A-64A, changing rooms

locations.name: Warsaw Uprising Museum
locations.setting: A former tram power station on Wola's Przyokopowa street, converted into a museum of the 1944 uprising, retaining its brick turbine hall and machinery among the exhibition spaces.

locations.name: Wieliczka Salt Mine
locations.setting: A working salt mine near Krakow dating to the 13th century, its tunnels reaching over 300 metres deep and including carved underground chapels and chambers open to visitors.
locations.known_for: On the Silver Globe (1988), Spellbinder: Land of the Dragon Lord (1997)

locations.name: Wielka Krokiew
locations.setting: A ski jumping hill and stadium on the edge of Zakopane, host of the Four Hills Tournament and of televised New Year's Eve concerts broadcast live from its outrun and stands.

locations.name: Wieża Ciśnień Katowice-Borki (Borki Water Tower)
locations.setting: A 66-metre brick water tower in the Borki district of Katowice, built 1911 to 1912 to a design by the Zillmann architecture studio and topped with a helmet-shaped dome.

locations.name: Wieza Cisnien water tower, Katowice-Borki
locations.setting: A 66 metre brick water tower in the Borki district of Katowice, designed in 1907 and built 1911-1912, with a circular 17 metre footprint and a dome shaped like a Prussian military helmet.

locations.name: Wrocław Świebodzki Railway Station
locations.setting: A disused 1843 railway terminus in Wrocław, closed to regular trains in 1991, now home to a stage of the Polish Theatre and a large Sunday flea market inside its restored hall.

locations.name: Adega Mayor
locations.setting: A contemporary winery building in Campo Maior, Alentejo, offering vineyard tours and tastings alongside its architecture, listed in Portugal Film Commission's location database.

locations.name: Alfama
locations.setting: Lisbon's oldest quarter, a hillside maze of steep cobbled lanes, tiled facades and tram lines above the Tagus.

locations.name: Algarve International Circuit
locations.setting: FIA-grade motor racing circuit near Portimao with elevation changes of up to forty metres, a start-finish straight, paddock buildings and grandstands.

locations.name: Armazéns do Chiado
locations.setting: A rebuilt 19th century department store in Lisbon's Chiado district, now a shopping centre behind its restored historic facade after the 1988 Chiado fire.

locations.name: Barbadinhos Steam Pumping Station
locations.setting: Steam-powered water pumping station in Xabregas that operated from 1880 to 1928, preserving four steam engines inside its industrial hall as part of Lisbon's water museum.

locations.name: Braga Municipal Stadium
locations.setting: Football stadium built into a disused granite quarry on Monte Castro, with seating on two sides only and the bare quarry rock face left exposed behind each goal.

locations.name: Casa da Musica
locations.setting: Angular concrete concert hall by Rem Koolhaas on Porto's Rotunda da Boavista, with a shoebox-shaped main auditorium and several smaller performance rooms.

locations.name: Casa de Mateus
locations.setting: Baroque manor house near Vila Real with formal box-hedge gardens and a cedar tunnel, pictured on the label of Mateus Rose wine and used as a venue for concerts and cultural events.

locations.name: Casa dos Patudos
locations.setting: Early twentieth-century manor house in Alpiarca designed by architect Raul Lino for collector Jose Relvas, with period interiors and furnishings now open as a museum.

locations.name: Castelo de Beja
locations.setting: A medieval castle with a tall keep in the town of Beja, southern Alentejo, catalogued among Portugal Film Commission's castle locations.

locations.name: Centro Português de Fotografia
locations.setting: Porto's former prison and law court building on Largo Amor de Perdição, now the national photography museum and archive, with its original cell wings preserved.

locations.name: Convento de Cristo
locations.setting: Templar castle and convent complex crowned by the round Charola oratory, with Manueline cloisters and hilltop ramparts above Tomar.
locations.known_for: The Man Who Killed Don Quixote (2018)

locations.name: Estacao do Rossio
locations.setting: Neo-Manueline railway station on Lisbon's Rossio square, with two horseshoe-arched doorways on its facade and platforms reached through a tunnel under the Bairro Alto hill.

locations.name: Estádio do Dragão
locations.setting: FC Porto's stadium in Campanhã, opened in 2003 with about 50,000 seats, offering pitch, stands, museum and hospitality areas.

locations.name: Evora Historic Centre
locations.setting: UNESCO-listed Alentejo city within Roman and medieval walls, with a Roman temple, whitewashed streets, a granite cathedral and the bone-lined Capela dos Ossos.

locations.name: Fábrica Braço de Prata
locations.setting: A former military ammunition factory in Marvila, Lisbon, converted into a cultural complex with a theatre, bar and exhibition halls across its old industrial buildings.

locations.name: Farol dos Capelinhos
locations.setting: Coastal lighthouse on Faial partly buried by ash from the 1957-58 Capelinhos submarine volcanic eruption, standing on the new lava and ash landscape it created.

locations.name: Herdade do Freixo
locations.setting: A rolling Alentejo wine estate near Redondo whose modern winery building won ArchDaily's Building of the Year in 2018, set among vineyards with wide viewpoints.

locations.name: Lousal Mining Museum
locations.setting: Former pyrite-mining village in Grandola built around a twentieth-century mining company's power plant, now a museum with mining machinery, tools and worker housing.

locations.name: Madeira Botanical Garden
locations.setting: Terraced hillside garden above Funchal with exotic and native plant collections on volcanic slopes, reached by road or by a cable car from Monte.

locations.name: Marvao
locations.setting: Walled hilltop village on the Spanish border in the Serra de Sao Mamede, with a castle, whitewashed houses and long views over the surrounding plain.

locations.name: Mercado do Bolhao
locations.setting: Porto's historic municipal market, reopened in 2022 after renovation, with two levels of fish, meat, flower and grocery stalls under a restored iron and glass roof.

locations.name: Mosteiro de São Martinho de Tibães
locations.setting: A Benedictine monastery complex near Braga with a baroque church, cloisters and gardens spanning eight centuries of building history, catalogued as a Portugal Film Commission location.

locations.name: Museu Nacional Ferroviario
locations.setting: National railway museum on the site of Entroncamento's railway works, with steam locomotives, carriages and workshop sheds spanning more than a century of Portuguese rail history.

locations.name: Piscina das Marés
locations.setting: Álvaro Siza's tidal swimming pools built into the rocks at Leça da Palmeira, Matosinhos, using seawater pools framed in board marked concrete.

locations.name: Portalegre Tapestry Museum (Guy Fino)
locations.setting: Tapestry museum inside a former noble town house in Portalegre, remodelled to display the local tapestry workshop's collection and archive alongside the original architecture.

locations.name: Porto de Leixões
locations.setting: The deep water port of Leixões between Matosinhos and Leça da Palmeira, with container terminals, a cruise terminal and breakwaters managed by port authority APDL.

locations.name: Praia do Guincho
locations.setting: Wide Atlantic surf beach backed by dunes and the Sintra hills, known for strong wind and heavy waves.

locations.name: Quinta do Pisao
locations.setting: Former farm estate on the edge of the Sintra-Cascais Natural Park, with old agricultural buildings, pine woods, pasture and a small lake open to visitors.

locations.name: Santa Cruz Municipal Aerodrome
locations.setting: Small municipal airfield close to the Santa Cruz beaches near Torres Vedras, home to the local aeroclub and one of the earliest civil aviation sites near Lisbon.

locations.name: Time Out Market Lisboa
locations.setting: The restored 1892 Mercado da Ribeira market hall by Cais do Sodré in Lisbon, now a large food hall with dozens of kitchens and counters under Time Out's management.

locations.name: University of Coimbra (Paco das Escolas)
locations.setting: UNESCO-listed royal-palace-turned-university courtyard in Coimbra, with the Joanina Baroque library, a bell tower and ceremonial halls still in academic use.

locations.name: Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas Airport
locations.setting: Madrid's main international airport, operated by Aena, with passenger terminals and airside areas listed under transport locations in the Madrid Film Office catalogue.

locations.name: Almaden Mining Park
locations.setting: A former mercury mine in Ciudad Real with headframes, shafts and underground galleries open for visits, worked from Roman times until closure in 2001.

locations.name: Anden 0 (Chamberi Ghost Station)
locations.setting: A disused 1919 Madrid Metro station preserved with its original tiled advertisements and platform furniture, opened to the public as a small museum called Anden 0.

locations.name: Auditorio de Tenerife
locations.region: Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Canary Islands
locations.setting: A sail-shaped concert hall on the Santa Cruz de Tenerife waterfront designed by Santiago Calatrava, with a curved white concrete shell around the main auditorium.
locations.facilities: More than 15 multi-purpose spaces for events, described as having over 100 different corners, equipped with technical facilities for conferences and events.
locations.suitability: Interior and exterior filming, photoshoots, vehicle catalogue shoots, fashion and advertising productions are hosted; enquiries go through a dedicated filming contact (localizaciones@auditoriodetenerife.com), separate from the general events and conferences contact.

locations.name: Azkuna Zentroa
locations.setting: A former wine and grain warehouse, the Alhondiga, in Bilbao rebuilt by Philippe Starck behind its original brick facade, with 43 varied columns under a rooftop pool and terrace.

locations.name: Bardenas Reales
locations.setting: A semi-desert badlands landscape in southern Navarre with eroded clay buttes, plateaus and canyons, crossed by marked tracks inside a managed nature reserve.

locations.name: Belchite (old town)
locations.setting: The ruined shell of a town destroyed in the 1937 Battle of Belchite, left standing as a memorial with intact facades, a bell tower and rubble-filled streets open to visitors.
locations.known_for: The Adventures of Baron Munchausen (1988), Pan's Labyrinth (2006)

locations.name: Bilbao Metro
locations.setting: A metro network known for Norman Foster's glass-tube station entrances, locally called fosteritos, running through Bilbao and under the Nervion estuary.

locations.name: Bombas Gens
locations.setting: A former water-pump factory in Valencia built in Art Deco style, its restored halls now an art foundation with gallery and workshop spaces.

locations.name: Camp Nou
locations.setting: FC Barcelona's stadium in the Les Corts district, one of Europe's largest football grounds, with tiered stands, a museum and tour access during redevelopment.
locations.facilities: The stadium includes a presidential box and VIP lounge, press rooms and television studios, and the FC Barcelona club museum.

locations.name: Canfranc International Railway Station
locations.setting: A Beaux-Arts railway station in the Pyrenees built for a cross-border line to France, its platforms and grand hall largely disused since 1970 and now under partial restoration.

locations.name: Casco Histórico y Mercado de Villa de Vallecas
locations.setting: The old quarter of Villa de Vallecas in southeast Madrid, with its historic square and adjoining municipal market, catalogued by Madrid Film Office for street and market scenes.

locations.name: Castillo de Almodóvar del Río
locations.setting: A restored medieval hilltop castle above the Guadalquivir in Almodóvar del Río, listed in Andalucía Film Commission's network of singular private venues.

locations.name: Centro Comercial Arturo Soria Plaza
locations.setting: A 7,000 square metre shopping centre in Ciudad Lineal with two retail floors, renovated in 2019, listed on the Madrid Film Office catalogue with production offices and loading access.
locations.facilities: Production offices, dressing rooms, catering space, storage, electric hookups, loading dock, parking

locations.name: City of Arts and Sciences
locations.setting: A cluster of white concrete and glass structures by Santiago Calatrava and Felix Candela beside the old Turia riverbed, including a planetarium dome, an opera house, a science museum and an oceanarium.
locations.facilities: Six buildings (Palau de les Arts Reina Sofia, Hemisferic, Museu de les Ciencies, Umbracle, Agora and Oceanografic) across a 350,000 m2 site along a two-kilometre axis.
locations.suitability: The complex's buildings have been used for business launches, photo shoots, feature films, advertising, catalogues and music videos, both indoors and outdoors, nationally and internationally.

locations.name: City of Culture of Galicia
locations.setting: A hilltop complex of curved stone and glass buildings by Peter Eisenman above Santiago de Compostela, combining library, museum and archive functions on wide open plazas.
locations.price_note: Space rental fees (own site, General tariff for private for-profit hire): Floor -1 hall (1,731 m2, up to 800 people) EUR 4,800/day; Fontan Auditorium (694 seats) EUR 2,100/day; CINC Convention Hall (250 people) EUR 1,250/day; Museum/Tirantes Hall (up to 300 people) EUR 1,800/day; outdoor squares and enclosures EUR 500/day; other indoor spaces EUR 600/day. A Reduced tariff for public bodies and non-profits is roughly half these rates.
locations.facilities: Nine main rentable spaces: the Fontan Auditorium (836 m2, 694 seats, dividable), CINC's Auditorium 1 (177 seats), Auditorium 2 (106 seats) and Convention Hall (250 people), the Gaias Centre Museum's Floor -1 hall (1,731 m2, up to 800 people in theatre layout) and Museum Hall (1,081 m2, up to 300 people for a cocktail reception), the Library's Xose Neira Vilas Auditorium (121 seats), meeting rooms from 26 to 168 m2 (8 to 50 people), and outdoor squares and enclosures.
locations.logistics: On-site covered parking is available at EUR 30/month.

locations.name: Ciudad de la Luz
locations.setting: Purpose-built studio complex beside the Mediterranean on the edge of Alicante, with large sound stages, exterior water tanks and production support buildings, reopened to shoots in 2022.
locations.known_for: Asterix at the Olympic Games (2008), The Impossible (2012)
locations.facilities: Six sound stages from 1,620 to 2,340 m2 (Plato 3: 2,340 m2 and 2,000 kVA; Plato 4: 1,794 m2; Platos 1, 2, 5 and 6: 1,620 m2, 12.5 m high, 10 x 8 m door, 1,250 kVA), interior tanks in Platos 3 and 5; an exterior 100 x 80 m water tank (8,000 m2, 1.2 m base, 5.2 m in a 30 x 30 m pit, 120 x 12 m green screen) with an infinity horizon to the Mediterranean; Backlot 1 of 42,367 m2 and Backlot 2 of 75,246 m2, each with 4,000 kVA; production buildings, workshops, storage, auditorium and post-production.
locations.suitability: Stages have NC-25 acoustic insulation and silent air conditioning; the tank offers up to 16 m underwater visibility, wave and water cannon systems and fills in 48 hours. 24-hour private security and access control let production teams work at any hour.
locations.logistics: On the edge of Alicante; the site cites an international airport nearby and Madrid under two hours by AVE high-speed train.

locations.name: Ciudad Encantada
locations.setting: A karst rock park near Cuenca where erosion has carved limestone into towers and shapes along a signed walking route through pine forest.

photo.author: Turol Jones, un artista de cojones from Villanueva del Cascajal, República Independiente de Mi Casa

locations.name: Ciudad Pegaso
locations.setting: A 1955 workers housing estate in San Blas-Canillejas with low rise apartment blocks, single family homes, a parish church and shared sports ground, catalogued by Madrid Film Office.
locations.suitability: Residential streets and building exteriors; filming permit issued through Madrid's Negociado de Autorizaciones de Rodajes.

locations.name: Complutense University of Madrid
locations.setting: A large 1930s university campus, Ciudad Universitaria, west of central Madrid, with monumental faculty buildings, an observatory and open lawns.

locations.name: Conde Duque
locations.setting: A former 18th-century army barracks in Madrid with a long baroque facade and large parade-ground courtyards, converted into a public cultural centre.
locations.price_note: Filming day rates set by Madrid Destino (own site, tariff effective July 2025) vary by room, e.g. Patio Central EUR 10,000/day for a commercial, EUR 7,000/day for a feature film or series, EUR 1,050/day for a short film or documentary; smaller rooms from EUR 1,000/day for a commercial. Technical equipment is not included in the published rate for the Auditorium/Concert Hall or the Assembly Hall (Salon de Actos).
locations.facilities: Rentable spaces include Sala de Bovedas 1 and 2 (basement), the Auditorio/Sala de Conciertos, Sala Polivalente/Cafeteria, Sala de Exposiciones 2, Patio Central, Patio Sur and Patio Norte (ground floor), a Teatro, Salon de Actos, two rehearsal rooms and the Terraza Mirador (first floor).
locations.suitability: Filming requests are handled by Madrid Film Office, with a minimum of 10 working days to process the contract, and use must be compatible with the centre's own programming.

locations.name: Corralejo Dunes Natural Park
locations.setting: A protected dune field and beach on the north coast of Fuerteventura, with shifting white sand hills managed by the island council.

locations.name: Estadio Mestalla
locations.setting: Valencia CF's stadium near the city centre, one of Spain's older large football grounds, with pitch, stands and hospitality areas available through the club.

locations.name: Estadio Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán
locations.setting: Sevilla FC's stadium in Nervión, built in 1958, with pitch, stands, dressing rooms, press areas and an adjoining sports complex of 13 pitches offered for filming.

locations.name: Euskalduna Palace
locations.setting: A congress and concert hall in Bilbao built in weathered steel on the site of the former Euskalduna shipyard, its shape referencing a ship's hull under construction.

locations.name: Fabra i Coats
locations.setting: A former 19th-century textile mill in Barcelona's Sant Andreu district, its long brick sheds and chimney now used as artist studios and a cultural centre.

locations.name: Fira de Barcelona (Montjuïc venue)
locations.setting: Barcelona's historic trade fair complex on Montjuïc by Plaça d'Espanya, with several exhibition halls and a central avenue used for conventions, launches and large events.

locations.name: Fuerteventura Airport
locations.setting: The island airport of Fuerteventura, operated by Aena, catalogued by Canary Islands Film Commission under its airport locations.

locations.name: Gran Teatre del Liceu
locations.setting: Barcelona's main opera house on La Rambla, with a gilded horseshoe auditorium, a grand foyer and a stage house rebuilt after a 1994 fire.

locations.name: Hospital de Sant Pau
locations.setting: A former working hospital in Barcelona built as a campus of Art Nouveau pavilions with domes, mosaics and underground connecting tunnels, now a monument and event venue.
locations.facilities: Event spaces in the Administration Pavilion: the Lluis Domenech i Montaner Room (170 m2), Sala Pau Gil (245 m2), Francesc Cambo room (245 m2), the Hipostyle Hall (465 m2, drinks reception up to 300 people), a Board room (109 m2), eight meeting rooms (six of 45 m2, two of 90 m2, the latter splittable), the 1902 Room with a private terrace, and outdoor garden areas.

locations.name: Hotel Alfonso XIII
locations.setting: A 1928 regionalista hotel built for the Ibero-American Exposition in Seville, with mudejar and baroque details, columned courtyards and a tower, listed in Andalucía Film Commission's network of singular venues.
locations.known_for: The Crown, Berlin, Lawrence of Arabia
locations.facilities: Standard electrical grid, production offices, limited technical parking, adjacent gardens

locations.name: La Model
locations.setting: Barcelona's former Model prison in the Eixample, closed in 2017 after 113 years, now a memorial space with courtyard tours ahead of redevelopment into public facilities and housing.

locations.name: La Térmica
locations.setting: A provincial council cultural centre in Málaga with halls, a courtyard and exhibition spaces used for screenings and events, available for external space bookings.

locations.name: Las Medulas
locations.setting: A red-cliffed landscape left by Roman open-cast gold mining, honeycombed with tunnels and covered in chestnut trees, managed as a protected heritage site in the Bierzo hills.

locations.name: Matadero Madrid
locations.setting: A former municipal slaughterhouse and cattle market beside the Manzanares river, its early 20th-century brick pavilions converted into galleries, studios and event spaces.
locations.price_note: Filming day rates set by Madrid Destino (own site, tariff effective July 2025) vary by space and production type, e.g. Nave 16 (complete) EUR 16,000/day for a commercial, EUR 12,500/day for a feature film or series, EUR 2,300/day for a short film or documentary; Plaza Matadero (A+B) EUR 8,750/day for a commercial, EUR 1,250/day for a short film or documentary. Half-day rates are about 60% of the full-day rate.
locations.facilities: Rentable filming spaces include Plaza Matadero (sections A and B, combinable), Nave 16 (full nave or modules), the Naves Teatro Espanol (Sala Fernando Arrabal, Sala Max Aub, Nave 12-Cafeteria), Sala 2, Terrario, Espacio Taller, and the Cineteca (Sala Azcona, Sala Borau, vestibule, set and archive).
locations.suitability: Filming requests are handled by Madrid Film Office (info@madridfilmoffice.com), with a minimum of 10 working days to process the contract once documentation is received. Use must be compatible with the centre's own programming, and outdoor areas stay open to the public and cannot be closed off entirely. A full filming day is a maximum of 12 hours; night sessions (up to 10 hours) carry a 25% surcharge and Sunday/holiday sessions a 40% surcharge, both subject to the centre's approval. Discounts of up to 100% apply for feature films, series, documentaries, shorts and music videos backed by ICAA or Comunidad/Ayuntamiento de Madrid, up to 90% for TV entertainment programmes, and up to 50% for advertising productions.
locations.logistics: The producer or organiser covers costs such as security, cleaning and supplies, and must take out an insurance policy covering the space's use.

locations.name: Mercado Central de Valencia
locations.setting: A 1928 Art Nouveau market hall in central Valencia with domed ceilings, stained glass and stalls trading under an iron and tile structure.

locations.name: Mercado de Colón
locations.setting: A 1916 modernist market hall in Valencia's Eixample designed by Francisco Mora, its original iron and glass structure now housing cafes and restaurants.

locations.name: Mercado de la Ribera
locations.setting: A large Art Deco covered market on the Nervión riverbank in Bilbao's old town, with several trading floors of food stalls.

locations.name: Mercado de San Miguel
locations.setting: A restored early 1900s cast-iron and glass market hall next to Plaza Mayor in Madrid, now a covered food and tapas market.

locations.name: Mercado Municipal de Vallehermoso
locations.setting: A 1930 municipal market hall in Chamberí with a coloured corner facade, its stalls and storage areas offered for filming outside main trading hours.
locations.facilities: Vehicle access, restricted loading hours, catering area, storage space, restrooms
locations.suitability: Best available Sunday evenings and Mondays; other schedules negotiable with the market.

locations.name: Mini Hollywood (Oasys Parque Tematico)
locations.setting: A preserved western film set in the Tabernas desert built for 1960s Spaghetti Westerns, with a saloon, jail and main street still used for stunt shows and shoots.
locations.known_for: A Fistful of Dollars (1964), For a Few Dollars More (1965)

locations.name: Museo del Ferrocarril de Madrid
locations.setting: Spain's railway museum, housed in the former Delicias terminus with its 19th-century iron and glass trainshed, displaying historic locomotives and carriages.

locations.name: Palacio de Cibeles / CentroCentro
locations.setting: Madrid's ornate former post office building on Plaza de Cibeles, now the city hall, with a public exhibition centre, a rooftop viewpoint and a domed central hall.
locations.price_note: Filming day rates set by Madrid Destino (own site, tariff effective July 2025) vary by room, e.g. Patio de Operaciones EUR 10,000/day for a commercial, EUR 7,000/day for a feature film or series, EUR 1,500/day for a short film or documentary; Galeria de Cristal EUR 9,200/day for a commercial. Half-day rates are about 60% of the full-day rate.
locations.facilities: Rentable rooms include the Galeria de Cristal, the Pasaje Galeria de Cristal, the Patio de Operaciones, the Auditorio Caja de Musica, the Mirador (7th floor), the Capilla, Carmen Santonja and Sigfrido Martin Begue rooms (2nd floor), the Jorge G. Berlanga room, an exhibition space on the 1st floor, and the Area Social (6th floor mezzanine).
locations.suitability: Filming requests are handled by Madrid Film Office, with a minimum of 10 working days to process the contract. Use must be compatible with the centre's own programming; cultural-interest filming or reporting about the centre's own activities can be authorised free of charge, while commercial filming that identifies the CentroCentro brand needs approval from the Artistic Direction and Management.

locations.name: Palacio Domecq
locations.setting: A historic sherry house palace in Jerez de la Frontera, listed in Andalucía Film Commission's network of singular private venues.

locations.name: Palau de la Musica Catalana
locations.setting: A Modernista concert hall in Barcelona by Lluis Domenech i Montaner, with a stained-glass skylight, sculpted facades and an ornate main auditorium.
locations.facilities: Rentable spaces listed are the Concert Hall, Petit Palau, Foyer, Rehearsal Hall, Lluis Millet Room and a Terrace.
locations.suitability: Space rental is offered specifically for filming and recordings, in addition to musical activities and corporate/social events, each with its own dedicated contact line.

locations.name: Palau Sant Jordi
locations.setting: An indoor arena on Montjuïc designed by Arata Isozaki for the 1992 Olympics, used for concerts, sports events and large productions.

locations.name: Playa de las Catedrales
locations.setting: A tidal beach at Ribadeo shaped by sea arches and cliffs up to 30 metres high, fully walkable only at low tide and reached with a free timed permit in summer.

photo.author: Jose Luis Cernadas Iglesias from Coruña, España

locations.name: Plaza de Toros de Las Ventas
locations.setting: Madrid's Neo-Mudejar bullring seating over 23,000, with brick and ceramic tile facades, tiered stands and an on-site bullfighting museum.

locations.name: Poblado Dirigido de San Cristóbal de los Ángeles
locations.setting: A 1959 social housing scheme in Villaverde built as open superblocks around courtyards, with two 12 and 14 storey towers and a surviving brick factory chimney, listed by Madrid Film Office.

locations.name: Puerto de Bilbao
locations.setting: The port of Bilbao at the mouth of the Nervión estuary, with container terminals, quaysides and breakwaters managed by the Bilbao Port Authority.

locations.name: Puerto de Las Palmas
locations.setting: The commercial and passenger port of Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, with quaysides, terminal buildings and the Santa Catalina wharf, catalogued by Canary Islands Film Commission's ports category.

locations.name: Real Alcázar of Seville
locations.setting: Mudéjar royal palace complex in central Seville with tiled courtyards, arched ceremonial halls and lush formal gardens.
locations.known_for: Lawrence of Arabia (1962), Kingdom of Heaven (2005), Game of Thrones (season 5, Dorne)

photo.author: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA. Edited by MenkinAlRire

locations.name: Riotinto Mining Park
locations.setting: An open-cast copper and mineral mining landscape in Huelva province with reddened terrain, a heritage mining railway and a mining museum.

locations.name: Riyadh Air Metropolitano
locations.setting: Atlético Madrid's stadium in San Blas-Canillejas, built with conference and event functions alongside football, offering outdoor areas for private functions.

locations.name: Royal Tapestry Factory
locations.setting: A working tapestry and carpet workshop in Madrid founded in 1721, still weaving on wooden looms in its original workshop halls, open for guided tours.

locations.name: Santiago Bernabeu Stadium
locations.setting: Real Madrid's stadium in central Madrid, seating over 80,000 under a retractable roof, with dressing rooms, a trophy room and pitch-level tour access.

locations.name: Soller Railway
locations.setting: A narrow-gauge heritage railway on Mallorca linking Palma to Soller through the Serra de Tramuntana, still running vintage wooden carriages dating from 1912.

locations.name: Tabakalera
locations.setting: A former state tobacco factory in San Sebastian, its early 20th-century industrial halls converted into a contemporary culture and creation centre.
locations.facilities: Ten rentable spaces: Patio (620 m2, 10 m high; banquet 220 / cocktail 600 / theatre 400), Cine hall (327 m2, 5 m high; theatre or classroom 229), Sala 1 (184 m2, 5.5 m high; banquet 80 / cocktail 120 / theatre 120 / classroom 80), Prisma + Terraza (309 + 139 m2; banquet 180 / cocktail 285 / theatre 200), Plaza (492 m2, 23-27 m high; banquet 180 / cocktail 430 / theatre 200), Nave 1 (211 m2, cocktail 220), Nave 2 (343 m2, cocktail 171), the film and audiovisual lab (265 m2, cocktail 130), Terraza Este (200 m2, outdoor, cocktail 200), and the first-floor Distribuidor (335 m2, cocktail 170).

locations.name: Tabernas Desert
locations.setting: Europe's only true desert, with eroded badlands, dry riverbeds and surviving western town sets from the spaghetti-western era.
locations.known_for: Lawrence of Arabia (1962), The Good, the Bad and the Ugly (1966), Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade (1989)

locations.name: Timanfaya National Park
locations.setting: A national park on Lanzarote covering volcanic terrain formed by 18th-century eruptions, with lava fields, craters and a visitor route by coach.

locations.name: Tower of Hercules
locations.setting: A still-operating Roman lighthouse on a headland outside A Coruna, the oldest lighthouse in continuous use in the world, refaced in granite in the 18th century.

locations.name: Túneles M-30
locations.setting: Underground service galleries and technical chambers within Madrid's M-30 ring road tunnels, reaching about 60 metres deep, made available by the road operator for corridor and underground scenes.
locations.logistics: Access via Calle Méndez Álvaro 95; arranged through the tunnel operator Madrid Calle 30.

locations.name: University of Alcala
locations.setting: A 16th-century university campus in Alcala de Henares, centred on the Colegio de San Ildefonso with its plateresque facade and a historic assembly hall.

locations.name: University of Salamanca
locations.setting: Spain's oldest university, with a 16th-century plateresque facade, cloisters and historic lecture halls set around Salamanca's old town.

locations.name: University of Seville (Rectorado)
locations.setting: Seville's university rectorate housed in the former Royal Tobacco Factory, an 18th-century industrial building with long stone facades, courtyards and vaulted halls.

locations.name: Vizcaya Bridge
locations.setting: A working transporter bridge over the Ria de Bilbao between Portugalete and Las Arenas, carrying a suspended gondola across the estuary since 1893, with a walkway on top.
locations.facilities: Rentable spaces include four open-air terraces above the estuary, the elevated walkway (Pasarela, 50 metres above the estuary), and the gondola (Barquilla, which carries an in-cabin TV channel running 24 hours a day), plus advertising spots (posters and shop-window displays) inside and outside the gondola.
locations.suitability: The bridge hosts private events such as parties and receptions on the open-air terraces or on the elevated walkway; marquees can also be rented for the terraces.

locations.name: Zona Industrial Villa de Vallecas
locations.setting: A small industrial pocket of Villa de Vallecas with narrow streets, warehouses and low workshop buildings on distinctive corner plots, catalogued by Madrid Film Office.

locations.name: Abisko National Park
locations.setting: National park in Swedish Lapland around Lake Tornetrask, with birch forest, mountain heath, the Abisko canyon and a mountain station used as a base for hiking and aurora viewing.

locations.name: Dalhalla
locations.setting: Open-air amphitheatre built into a flooded former limestone quarry near Rattvik in Dalarna, with a stage, restaurant and glamping accommodation beside the water.
locations.facilities: Restaurant, glamping tents, transfer buses for events

locations.name: Falu Gruva (Falun Mine)
locations.setting: UNESCO-listed copper mine in Falun, Dalarna, with underground tour routes, a mine museum, historic miners' cottages and a large open pit.

locations.name: Fårö
locations.setting: Small Baltic island north of Gotland with limestone rauk stacks, shingle shores and windswept heathland, where Ingmar Bergman lived and filmed for decades.
locations.known_for: Persona (1966), Through a Glass Darkly (1961), Scenes from a Marriage (1973)

locations.name: Film i Väst
locations.setting: Regional film fund and studio base in Trollhättan, nicknamed Trollywood, whose stages and industrial halls have held full-scale purpose-built sets.
locations.price_note: Studio Fares SEK 25,000 for the first day and SEK 20,000 per following day, plus 25 percent VAT (own site)
locations.facilities: Studio Fares: one 1,100 m2 sound stage (31.3 x 36.1 m, 10 m to the gallery) with a telfer system of 40 hoists, 1,000 A permanent power plus 1,000 A temporary, and doors 4.5 m high; props storage, carpentry workshop, production offices with 26 desks on two floors, three dressing rooms, makeup and wardrobe and a 50-seat cafe with kitchen.
locations.suitability: Rented primarily to Film i Vast co-productions under a licence agreement; external bookings are accepted at most two months ahead. The rent includes utilities, parking, cleaning and use of the facilities.
locations.logistics: Trollhattan; gated, secure parking with four EV charging points. Website in Swedish only.

locations.name: Filmhuset
locations.setting: The Brutalist 1970 headquarters of the Swedish Film Institute in Gardet, Stockholm, built to resemble a camera, housing a film archive, offices and two public cinemas.
locations.known_for: Guldbagge Awards ceremony, Stockholm International Film Festival industry programme
locations.facilities: Two cinemas (Bio Victor and Bio Mauritz) available for public rental, a large film archive, open plan offices

locations.name: Icehotel
locations.setting: Hotel rebuilt each winter from ice and snow from the Torne River in Jukkasjarvi, Swedish Lapland, alongside a year-round warm wing, with conference and wedding facilities.
locations.facilities: Conference and events facilities, weddings program

locations.name: Kulturhuset Stadsteatern
locations.setting: Culture house and municipal theatre on Sergels torg in central Stockholm, with several stages, exhibition halls, a library and rooms available for hire.
locations.facilities: Spaces listed for hire: Foajé 3, Hörsalen, Klarabiografen (cinema), Lilla studion, Studion and the galleries.

locations.name: Langholmen
locations.setting: Former state prison on a small island in central Stockholm, closed in 1975 and converted into a hotel, hostel and restaurant that keeps its original cell wings.
locations.facilities: Hotel, hostel, restaurant and conference rooms in former cell wings

locations.name: Lindholmen
locations.setting: Former shipyard peninsula in Gothenburg redeveloped since the 1990s into a science park of offices, test beds and studios jointly run by the city and industry.

locations.name: Liseberg
locations.setting: Amusement park in central Gothenburg with rides, stages and gardens, plus on-site hotels and dedicated conference and event spaces for hire.
locations.facilities: Conference spaces at the park, Lisebergsbyn and Grand Curiosa Hotel

locations.name: Malmo Live
locations.setting: Concert hall and congress centre in Malmo, home to the Malmo Symphony Orchestra, with a main concert hall and several smaller performance spaces.
locations.logistics: Stage entry at Beringsgatan 5; loading access at Beringsgatan 1-3; visiting address Dag Hammarskjölds torg 4, Malmo.

locations.name: Royal Swedish Opera
locations.setting: National opera and ballet house on Gustav Adolfs torg in Stockholm, founded in 1773, with a 19th-century auditorium due for renovation from 2027.
locations.facilities: The Golden Foyer, the space published for hire, seats up to 120 or holds up to 200 standing, and includes a terrace overlooking Gustav Adolfs torg, weather permitting.

locations.name: Skansen
locations.setting: Open-air museum on Djurgarden in Stockholm, the oldest of its kind in the world, with about 190 historic buildings relocated from across Sweden plus a zoo.
locations.facilities: Business bookings and bookable group experiences

locations.name: Slagthuset
locations.setting: A former municipal abattoir in Malmo's harbour district converted into an event venue, keeping its industrial brick halls for concerts, conferences and large private functions.

locations.name: Universeum
locations.setting: Sweden's national science centre in Gothenburg, a ten-floor building with rainforest and ocean exhibits, a visualisation dome and dedicated event and conference spaces.
locations.facilities: Published event packages: dinner and drinks in the Ocean zone (max 250), dinner with Wisdome show (max 250), conference (max 30), and hire of the entire venue (over 500).

locations.name: Vasa Museum
locations.setting: Maritime museum on Djurgarden in Stockholm built around the salvaged 17th-century warship Vasa, which sank on its maiden voyage in 1628.
locations.facilities: Ship Hall, the main event space next to the ship Vasa: up to 800 guests seated for dinner or up to 2,000 for a standing reception. Adjoining restaurant: up to 150 guests seated or standing.

locations.name: Visby
locations.setting: Medieval walled town on Gotland and a UNESCO World Heritage site, with a 3.4 kilometre town wall, cobbled lanes and ruined medieval churches.

locations.name: Ystad
locations.setting: Medieval coastal town with half-timbered houses, cobbled streets and a sandy Baltic shoreline, home to the Ystad Studios film facility.

locations.name: Aerospace Bristol
locations.setting: Aviation museum on the former Filton airfield site with a hangar housing a preserved Concorde alongside earlier Bristol-built aircraft.

locations.name: Amberley Museum
locations.setting: Open-air industrial heritage museum on a former chalk quarry near Arundel, with narrow-gauge railways, a lime works, workshops and period industrial buildings.

locations.name: Arbeia Roman Fort
locations.setting: A reconstructed Roman fort and supply base at South Shields, with a rebuilt gatehouse, barrack blocks and commanding officer's house on the original foundations.
locations.suitability: Part of the North East Museums group, which states it welcomes film, television and photography companies to hire its venues

locations.name: Audley End House and Gardens
locations.setting: Jacobean mansion near Saffron Walden remodelled in the eighteenth century, with state rooms, a service wing and Capability Brown parkland.

locations.name: Ayr Racecourse
locations.setting: Scotland's principal racecourse on the Ayrshire coast, with grandstands, a parade ring and parkland hired for events between race meetings.

locations.name: Barrowland Ballroom
locations.setting: Category B listed 1930s dance hall and live music venue in Glasgow's East End, with its original sprung floor and a neon sign facade on the Gallowgate.

locations.name: Battersea Power Station
locations.setting: Decommissioned Thames-side coal power station with four white chimneys, its turbine halls and boiler house now restored inside a mixed-use redevelopment.
locations.known_for: The King's Speech, Children of Men
locations.facilities: Event spaces include Control Room A (max 220 people), the Arcade Food Hall (max 600) and The Cinema in The Power Station (max 350).

locations.name: Beamish Museum
locations.setting: Open-air museum in County Durham recreating a Georgian, Victorian and 1950s north-east England landscape with a working colliery, tramway, town street and farm.

locations.name: Belfast City Hall
locations.setting: Baroque Revival city hall of 1906 in central Belfast, with a domed rotunda, marble entrance hall, council chamber and banqueting hall.
locations.facilities: Great Hall: theatre 500, round dinner 400 (40 tables), standing reception 500. Banqueting Hall: theatre 225, round dinner 150 (15 tables), standing reception 250. Reception Room: theatre 100, round dinner 80 (8 tables), standing reception 120. Event spaces are on the first floor and accessible to visitors with disabilities.
locations.logistics: Booking requires a completed booking form at least eight weeks before the proposed event; applications are reviewed monthly by the Strategic Policy and Resources Committee.

locations.name: Belfast Harbour Studios
locations.setting: Purpose-built film and television studio complex on Belfast's Queen's Island, including the former Paint Hall shipyard building converted into sound stages.

locations.name: Big Pit National Coal Museum
locations.setting: Former working coal mine at Blaenavon in the South Wales valleys, part of a World Heritage industrial landscape, with pithead buildings and an underground tour.
locations.suitability: Written permission is required before using images or film in any commercial capacity; commercial shoots must be arranged in advance with the in-house team (venuehire@museumwales.ac.uk). Flash, camera supports and selfie sticks are not permitted without prior permission, and areas marked 'no photography or filming' are off-limits.

locations.name: Birmingham Hippodrome
locations.setting: Edwardian theatre in Birmingham's Southside, a working proscenium arch auditorium with a fly tower, used for touring opera, ballet and musicals.

locations.name: Bodleian Library
locations.setting: Historic university library in central Oxford with the vaulted Divinity School and Duke Humfrey's medieval reading room, hired for filming by arrangement.
locations.known_for: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets

locations.name: Borough Market
locations.setting: Covered Victorian food market south of London Bridge with wrought-iron arcades, market stalls and surrounding cobbled streets.
locations.known_for: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Bridget Jones's Diary
locations.suitability: Personal photography and small content-creator crews (handheld, max 2 people) do not need permission. Professional crews or commercial filming need written permission from the Market with at least 14 days notice, via a request form covering purpose, crew size, equipment and dates/times. Long-lensed cameras and tripods are not permitted for personal photography.
locations.logistics: Address: 8 Southwark Street, London SE1 1TL.

locations.name: Bressingham Steam and Gardens
locations.setting: Steam preservation site near Diss with narrow-gauge railways, a collection of traction engines and steam locomotives, and surrounding show gardens.

locations.name: Bristol Old Vic
locations.setting: Working eighteenth-century theatre in central Bristol, one of the oldest continuously operating in the English-speaking world, with a Georgian auditorium and backstage spaces.

locations.name: Brooklands Museum
locations.setting: Site of the world's first purpose-built motor racing circuit near Weybridge, with a surviving banked track section, aircraft hangars and early aviation and motoring exhibits.
locations.price_note: Charge applies for filming and photography on site; rates are discussed once an enquiry is made (own site)
locations.facilities: Edwardian Grade II listed Clubhouse (1907); Aircraft Factory hangar with a Wellington Bomber; Flight Shed with a Hawker Harrier and Sopwith Camel; Barnes Wallis-designed Stratosphere Chamber (1946); Aircraft Park including Concorde; Jackson Shed with historic F1 cars; Racing Sheds; the original 1907 motor racing circuit.
locations.suitability: Filming welcomed outside opening hours where possible; daytime filming possible on weekdays but no filming inside the Museum at weekends. Crews must hold public liability insurance of at least GBP 10m and provide risk assessments, method statements and a signed contract. Requests should be made at least two weeks in advance.
locations.logistics: Located between Weybridge and Byfleet, Surrey, a few minutes from Junction 10 of the M25 and the A3, about 30 minutes by train from London Waterloo. Free on-site parking, a cafe, and areas usable as dressing rooms, green rooms and production offices; catering can be arranged for out-of-hours filming.

locations.name: Butser Ancient Farm
locations.setting: Open-air archaeological site near Chalton with reconstructed Iron Age roundhouses, a Roman villa and Anglo-Saxon buildings set in working farmland.

locations.name: Charlestown Harbour
locations.setting: Small Georgian-era dry-dock harbour near St Austell, still used by tall ships, with quayside cottages and period pilchard cellars around the basin.
locations.facilities: Inner Harbour is 151m long, 33m wide and 5m deep, holding over 5,400 sq m of water; vessels up to 75m length and 4m draught can sail in directly from the open sea; described as one of the largest marine filming tanks in the world with access to open sea.
locations.suitability: Unspoilt South Cornish coastline location providing shelter from adverse marine conditions, enabling 'at sea' footage to be shot in rough weather; marine coordination, rigging services and prop hire available on site.
locations.logistics: Address: Charlestown Harbour, St Austell, Cornwall PL25 3NT.

locations.name: Cheddar Gorge
locations.setting: England's largest gorge, with 130-metre limestone cliffs, show caves and a clifftop footpath managed as part of the Longleat Estate.

locations.name: Chiswick Park
locations.setting: A landscaped west London business park of glass office buildings around a lake, promoted by its operator as a filming location for adverts and corporate shoots.

locations.name: Cliveden
locations.setting: Italianate mansion above the Thames at Taplow, now a hotel, with formal parterre gardens, a walled garden and woodland grounds managed by the National Trust.

locations.name: Colne Valley Railway
locations.setting: Heritage standard-gauge railway on the Essex-Suffolk border with a rebuilt country station, signal box and steam and diesel locomotives.

locations.name: Conwy Suspension Bridge
locations.setting: 1826 Thomas Telford suspension bridge across the Conwy estuary in north Wales, beside Conwy Castle, with its original tollhouse kept furnished.

locations.name: Copper Box Arena
locations.setting: A copper clad multi sport arena built for the 2012 Olympics in Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park, with a sprung floor hall hired for filming, sport and events.

locations.name: Cotswold Farm Park
locations.setting: A working rare breeds farm in the Cotswolds founded by broadcaster Adam Henson, with barns, fields and animal enclosures across open hillside.

locations.name: Coventry Transport Museum
locations.setting: Museum in central Coventry holding one of the largest collections of British-made cars, motorcycles and bicycles, with large open display halls.

locations.name: Crossness Pumping Station
locations.setting: A Victorian sewage pumping station in south east London, its ornate cast iron interior housing a restored beam engine and hired for filming.

locations.name: Crumlin Road Gaol
locations.setting: Former Victorian prison in north Belfast, closed in 1996, with its radial cell wings, a tunnel to the courthouse and an execution chamber preserved for tours and hire.

locations.name: Cutty Sark
locations.setting: A preserved nineteenth century tea clipper in dry dock at Greenwich, its decks, rigging and cargo hold open for events and location hire.

locations.name: Dean Clough
locations.setting: Former Crossley's carpet mill complex in Halifax, a chain of Victorian stone mill buildings around courtyards now used as offices, galleries and studios.

locations.name: Digbeth Loc. Studios
locations.setting: Purpose-built television and film studio complex in the Digbeth district of Birmingham with multiple sound stages and production offices.

locations.name: Discovery Museum
locations.setting: A free museum in Newcastle housed in Blandford House, an Edwardian former Co-operative Wholesale Society warehouse, with galleries and a turbine ship on display.
locations.suitability: Part of the North East Museums group, which states it welcomes film, television and photography companies to hire its venues

locations.name: Dreamland Margate
locations.setting: A restored 1920s seaside amusement park on the Kent coast with a wooden scenic railway and vintage rides, used as a period seaside backdrop.

locations.name: Dyrham Park
locations.setting: Baroque country house near Bath set in a steep deer park, with panelled state rooms, a Delftware collection and a walled garden.

locations.name: Eden Project
locations.setting: Environmental attraction built into a former china clay pit near St Austell, with two giant geodesic biome domes housing rainforest and Mediterranean planting.

locations.name: Elstree Studios
locations.setting: Film and television studio complex at Borehamwood with several sound stages, dating back to the 1920s and long used for major British productions.
locations.known_for: Star Wars, Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade

locations.name: Falkirk Wheel
locations.setting: A rotating boat lift connecting two canals near Falkirk, managed by Scottish Canals with a visitor centre, basin and towpaths around it.

locations.name: Fort Amherst
locations.setting: Napoleonic-era fortification above Chatham with brick ramparts, gun batteries and a network of tunnels cut into the chalk.

locations.name: Freshwater West
locations.setting: Wide Atlantic surf beach backed by dunes and low cliffs on the open Pembrokeshire coast.
locations.known_for: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows: Part 1, Robin Hood (2010), Their Finest

locations.name: Fulham Palace
locations.setting: Moated former residence of the Bishop of London beside the Thames at Putney, combining Tudor courtyards, Georgian rooms and walled gardens available for filming.
locations.facilities: Tudor courtyard, Georgian rooms and 13 acres of garden.
locations.suitability: Welcomes large filming projects as well as smaller photoshoots. Interior locations include the Great Hall, Chapel, Bishop Porteus's Library and drawing rooms.
locations.logistics: Described as easily accessible by London public transport.

locations.name: Geevor Tin Mine
locations.setting: Former working tin mine on the Cornish coast near Pendeen, with headframes, processing mills, underground tunnels and dressing floors preserved as a museum.

locations.name: Glenfinnan Viaduct
locations.setting: Curved 21-arch concrete railway viaduct of 1901 carrying the West Highland Line above the head of Loch Shiel.
locations.known_for: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban

locations.name: Here East
locations.setting: A converted Olympic press and broadcast centre beside the canal in Hackney Wick, now offices, television studios and workshop space.

locations.name: Hylands House
locations.setting: Neoclassical villa near Chelmsford set in landscaped parkland, with Regency reception rooms available for filming and events.

locations.name: Ikon Gallery
locations.setting: Contemporary art gallery in a restored Victorian board school building in Birmingham's Brindleyplace, with galleries, a tower and a public square outside.
locations.facilities: Victorian building with versatile spaces accommodating 10 to 500 guests (own site).

locations.name: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum
locations.setting: Red sandstone Edwardian museum and art gallery in Glasgow's West End, with an organ-fitted central hall, galleries and a park setting beside the River Kelvin.
locations.suitability: Commercial filming and sound recording requires permission from Glasgow Life (contact glasgowmuseumshire@glasgowlife.org.uk); personal filming/photography equipment such as selfie sticks, tripods, monopods, gimbals and lighting is not allowed.

locations.name: Kempton Park Racecourse
locations.setting: A Jockey Club racecourse near Sunbury with grandstands, a parade ring and open parkland, hired for filming and photography between race meetings.

locations.name: Knole
locations.setting: Sprawling calendar house near Sevenoaks with medieval and Tudor courtyards, a deer park and largely unaltered seventeenth-century state rooms.

locations.name: Landguard Fort
locations.setting: Coastal artillery fort at the mouth of the River Orwell near Felixstowe, rebuilt in stages from the seventeenth to the twentieth century with gun casemates and magazines.

locations.name: Leeds Corn Exchange
locations.setting: A domed Victorian former corn trading hall in Leeds city centre, now independent shops and studio units under a cast iron and glass roof.

locations.name: Littledean Jail
locations.setting: A former Victorian prison and police lock up in the Forest of Dean, now a museum with original cell blocks and a courtroom.

locations.name: Loseley Park
locations.setting: Elizabethan mansion near Guildford with panelled state rooms, a walled garden and surrounding parkland, hired for filming.
locations.known_for: Bridget Jones's Diary, The Wedding Date
locations.facilities: The Great Hall has oak panelling and an imposing fireplace; the Tithe Barn is a restored 17th-century barn with high beams; outdoor grounds and gardens are also available.
locations.suitability: Used as a filming location for period dramas, television series and feature films, citing its architectural heritage and landscapes.

locations.name: Manchester Central Convention Complex
locations.setting: Former Manchester Central railway station, a wrought iron and glass Victorian train shed converted into an exhibition and convention venue in the city centre.

locations.name: MediaCityUK
locations.setting: A media and business campus on Salford Quays with BBC and ITV studios, offices and waterside plazas, including the purpose built Coronation Street set, used for broadcast and corporate productions.

locations.name: Mitchell Library
locations.setting: Edwardian domed public reference library in Glasgow, one of Europe's largest, with a grand entrance hall, reading rooms and function spaces.

locations.name: Museum of the Gorge, Ironbridge
locations.setting: Former riverside warehouse at Ironbridge, part of the Ironbridge Gorge World Heritage Site of 18th century ironworking remains along the River Severn.

locations.name: National Justice Museum
locations.setting: Former courthouse and prison in Nottingham's Lace Market, with Georgian courtrooms, Victorian cells and a medieval undercroft, now a museum of law and punishment.

locations.name: National Railway Museum
locations.setting: National collection of historic locomotives and rolling stock in York, housed in former railway engine sheds with large open halls and turntables.
locations.facilities: Great Hall (up to 1,000 guests) displays locomotives including Mallard, Flying Scotsman and a Bullet Train; Station Hall (up to 450 guests) features Royal Carriages; two conference rooms with breakout areas accommodate up to 100 delegates. MIA Accredited Venue.
locations.logistics: Address: Leeman Road, York YO26 4XJ.

locations.name: National Slate Museum
locations.setting: A former slate quarry workshop at Llanberis in Snowdonia, with working machinery, a giant waterwheel and quarrymen's cottages preserved on site.

locations.name: National Space Centre
locations.setting: A space science museum in Leicester with a distinctive rocket tower, planetarium and exhibition halls, available for venue hire including production use.

locations.name: No.1 Royal Crescent
locations.setting: End-of-terrace Georgian townhouse on Bath's Royal Crescent, restored and furnished as a museum showing how it looked in the 1700s.
locations.facilities: Grand Georgian townhouse with interior rooms furnished in period style, including the Kitchen, Servants' Hall, Withdrawing Room, Dining Room, Lady's Bedroom, Housekeeper's Room and Gentleman's Bedroom.
locations.suitability: Interior rooms and the exterior can both be filmed; green room spaces and facilities are available; the museum can be hired in its entirety so filming is not interrupted by visitors. For filming along the wider Royal Crescent, the site directs enquiries to the Bath Film Office.

locations.name: Old Billingsgate
locations.setting: The former Victorian fish market hall on the Thames in the City of London, a column free riverside space hired for productions and functions.

locations.name: Old Royal Naval College
locations.setting: Baroque waterfront complex of colonnaded courts and a domed Painted Hall at Greenwich, hired as a stand-in for period Paris, Victorian London and other settings.
locations.known_for: Bridgerton, The Crown, Les Misérables, Thor
locations.suitability: Site accommodates documentary and commercial filming, personal and commercial photography, wedding photography, and news and media; featured in more than 300 productions including Bridgerton, The Crown, Les Miserables and Thor. Location fees charged go towards preserving the site.

locations.name: Orford Ness
locations.setting: Shingle spit on the Suffolk coast used for decades as a secret military testing site, with derelict laboratories, pagoda-shaped test buildings and a lighthouse.

locations.name: Park Hill
locations.setting: Grade II* listed 1960s brutalist housing estate overlooking Sheffield city centre, its long deck-access blocks partly restored and partly awaiting refurbishment.

locations.name: People's History Museum
locations.setting: The national museum of democracy in Manchester, housed in a former Edwardian hydraulic pumping station beside the River Irwell, with galleries and an events space.

locations.name: Perth Racecourse
locations.setting: A Scottish jump racing course set in Scone Palace Park near Perth, with grandstands and parkland offered for film and television location filming.
locations.suitability: Film and TV location filming advertised as a dedicated service alongside weddings and corporate hire

locations.name: Peterhead Prison Museum
locations.setting: Former Scottish state prison at Peterhead, closed in 2013, with its original cell blocks, exercise yard and perimeter wall open as a museum.
locations.facilities: Spaces include A Hall, the Segregation Block, the Booking In Office, the hospital wing, laundry and a woodwork area; over 125 years of prison history as backdrop.
locations.suitability: Used for crime dramas, documentaries and period productions; TV, film and photography productions are accommodated with flexible hire options and on-site support.

locations.name: Pinewood Studios
locations.setting: Major studio complex west of London whose facilities include large sound stages, the vast 007 Stage, backlots and an underwater filming tank.
locations.known_for: No Time to Die, Star Wars: The Force Awakens
locations.facilities: 30 stages including the 007 Stage (59,092 sq ft, 5,490 m2, 12 m high, with a 91 x 22 m interior tank 2 m deep), an underwater stage with a 20 x 10 x 6 m tank of 1.2 million litres kept at 30 C, three backlots (Paddock Lot, North Lot) with a 32,000 sq ft water pad, workshops of 1,000 to 12,000 sq ft, production offices, hair and makeup rooms, six mixing theatres and 20 cutting rooms.
locations.suitability: Stages are hired individually or in combination; an Indie Film Hub keeps two stages for independent film, over 150 on-lot businesses supply equipment hire, motion capture and 3D scanning, and Diving Services UK manages the underwater stage. Canteen, bar, cinema and 24/7 security on the lot.
locations.logistics: Pinewood Road, Iver Heath: 10 miles from Heathrow, via M4 junction 5 or A40 junction 1; about 45 minutes from Baker Street by Underground to Uxbridge then 10 minutes by taxi, with a free shuttle bus to Uxbridge, Slough, Gerrards Cross and West Ruislip stations; on-site parking.

locations.name: Portmeirion
locations.setting: Italianate village on the Gwynedd coast built by Clough Williams-Ellis between 1925 and 1975, with pastel-coloured buildings, a piazza and subtropical gardens.

locations.name: Portsmouth Historic Dockyard
locations.setting: Working Royal Navy dockyard and heritage site with historic warships, dry docks and Georgian storehouses along Portsmouth Harbour.

locations.name: Racecourse Ground
locations.setting: Football stadium in Wrexham, north Wales, one of the oldest international football grounds still in use, with stands close to the pitch on all four sides.

locations.name: Rhondda Heritage Park
locations.setting: A former colliery in the Rhondda valley, South Wales, preserved with pithead buildings and winding gear as a mining heritage museum.

locations.name: Ribblehead Viaduct
locations.setting: 24-arch stone railway viaduct carrying the Settle to Carlisle line across open moorland in the Yorkshire Dales.

locations.name: Riverside Museum
locations.setting: A Zaha Hadid designed transport museum where the Kelvin meets the Clyde in Glasgow, with a zigzag roofline, a recreated street and a tall ship moored outside.
locations.suitability: Photography, filming and sketching permitted under Glasgow Life's museum guidelines, with venue hire available

locations.name: Royal Albert Hall
locations.setting: Circular Victorian concert hall with a domed glass and iron roof, tiered galleries and a large stage, available for filming and photography by arrangement.
locations.known_for: The Man Who Knew Too Much, The King's Speech

locations.name: Royal Highland Centre
locations.setting: A large showground and exhibition centre at Ingliston near Edinburgh Airport, with halls, arenas and outdoor space hired for events and productions.

locations.name: Royal Holloway, University of London
locations.setting: Victorian university campus at Egham centred on the ornate French Renaissance-style Founder's Building, with quadrangles, a chapel and a picture gallery.
locations.suitability: Filming location services are offered alongside event spaces, catering and accommodation (own site).

locations.name: Salts Mill
locations.setting: Former Victorian textile mill in the Saltaire World Heritage village near Bradford, a vast stone and iron structure now used as galleries, shops and offices.
